evidence.text: On 9 September 2026 M+C Saatchi announced that the Parc-backed management buyout of its Australia and New Zealand advertising agency had failed due diligence and that the business will instead CEASE OPERATIONS before the end of 2026, with the entire ANZ leadership team and all staff departing and Woolworths finishing in November. There is no RNS on the subject -- not for the 22 July MBO agreement and not for the 9 September collapse and closure -- and no UK financial outlet has covered it. The 22 September interim statement is the first regulated document in which the UK market can see it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Australia has been the line that moves this stock. The 18 Sep 2025 interims, which carried the Australian restructure and the closure of the Bohemia media unit, produced -12.24% -- by far the largest of the 13 observed reactions (median |move| 1.98%). The 24 Nov 2025 trading update, which downgraded the FY25 decline to 7%, produced -5.16%. But the 20 Apr 2026 FY results, which disclosed FY25 separately-disclosed items of GBP9.1m 'largely restructuring costs in Australia' alongside the language 'simplify the businesses ... unlock the intrinsic value', produced +3.91%. So this line has moved the stock hard in both directions, and the sign has tracked whether Australia was presented as a continuing problem or as a problem being removed. This time it is being removed entirely.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Investegate RNS record for M&C Saatchi from 1 July 2026 to 21 September 2026 contains nothing but Transaction in Own Shares, three Holding(s) in Company and the Notice of Half Year Results -- no announcement of the MBO, none of its collapse, none of the closure. Every outlet carrying it is Australian trade press (Campaign Brief, Campaign Brief NZ, Campaign Brief Asia, Mumbrella, Mediaweek, B&T, Mi3). Sharecast covered this issuer's March 2026 CEO change, so it follows the name, and it did not carry this. If the market had priced the closure of an entire country's advertising operations announced with no consideration and all staff departing, the stock would not be sitting at 147p on 21 September, within 2% of its 52-week high of 150p and up 29% from its April low of 113.5p; nor would a break-up activist have crossed 9% on 18 September. What the tape shows instead is a 149p-to-142p drift from 8 to 11 September fully given back by 18 September on ordinary volume -- consistent with a handful of holders reading the Australian trade press, not with the information being in the price. Size: APAC was 18% of FY25 like-for-like group net revenue (GBP204.7m) and fell 22.3%, 'predominantly Australia'; Australia alone fell 31.9% and accounts for the whole gap between the -3.1% group decline ex-Australia and the -7.3% including it. Removing it structurally lifts continuing-group organic growth by roughly 3-4pp and lifts margin; against that sit closure costs on top of FY25's GBP9.1m of separately-disclosed items (largely Australian restructuring), cash out rather than in, and an FY27 consensus of GBP221.8m / +3.6% organic that has to come down on the revenue line. That two-sidedness is why the band spans -4.5 to +5.5 and the point estimate is only +1.2. Net of the rest of the company: this rests on one region, and it requires H1 net revenue and margin to be at least in line, which the 11 June AGM update (Jan-Apr, LFL net revenue in line and supportive of the full year outlook) and an easy cost comparative support -- H1 2025 LFL operating margin was 9.9% after first-half-weighted investment in senior talent that has since annualised, and group central costs fell from GBP12.4m to GBP6.1m.
evidence.independence: Independently reported the same day by Mumbrella ('M&C Saatchi is preparing to exit Australia, ending a 30-year run'; 'the Australian business will be folded by November'; 'Woolworths will be the last remaining client ... with its contract ending in November') at https://mumbrella.com.au/mc-saatchi-australia-set-to-close-936541 , and by Campaign Brief Asia at https://campaignbriefasia.com/2026/09/09/mc-saatchi-australia-new-zealand-advertising-agency-management-buyout-no-longer-proceeding/ . The underlying Australian deterioration is corroborated in the issuer's own primary document: the FY25 preliminary results state 'APAC: Net revenue fell 22.3% as the macroeconomic environment in the core Australia market remained very weak' and 'The Group closed its Australian media buying business in September 2025' -- https://www.mcsaatchiplc.com/~/media/Files/M/mc-saatchi/documents/result-centre/2025/fy-2025-results-announcement.pdf

Harwood has been publicly urging a BREAK-UP of M&C Saatchi since March 2026 and has stepped its stake up four times this year: 6.001% -> 7.118% (8 May) -> 8.023% (11 June) -> 9.0865% (18 September).

What there is: the three previous Harwood step-ups (12 May, 15 June, 5 August window) landed on ordinary days and moved nothing visible, which is the point -- none of them coincided with a catalyst. The comparable line is governance news, and the 9 March 2026 announcement of the CEO's departure with Vin Murria returning as deputy chair was the trigger for a re-rating from 113.5p in April to 150p in September.

It is also arithmetically a real purchase and not a buyback artefact: the 2,222,500 shares cancelled under the programme only take 9,700,000 shares from 8.023% to 8.081% of the reduced 120,034,965 voting rights, so Harwood genuinely bought 1,207,000 shares between 11 June and 18 September. Against a median 20-day turnover of USD264,728 (about GBP198k, roughly 135,000 shares a day at 146.7p) that is about nine days of the entire market's volume in this stock, and 274,644 shares traded on 21 September against a 20-day median near 135,000. consensus.basis: Sell-side coverage, carried because it is the measurable proxy for this stage's thesis. Phase 1 measured 1-2 analysts below $1m/day of turnover, 5-7 at $1-5m, 11-13 at $5-25m and 16-19 above, consistently across all three markets. eu_resolve.py ranks the hunt BY this band so the thesis is tested rather than selected on.

history.caveat: Dates are REAL: each row is a results announcement the market's own archive records on that date, and the move is over this stage's own window. Only the UK (Investegate) and Norway (Oslo NewsWeb) reach this state; the other eight markets are estimated.

event_plausibility.basis: vendor forward calendar (TradingView), measured at a 2.2% phantom rate on 90 UK rows against the RNS record. Confirmation against Investegate (RNS mirror) is eu_resolve.py's job, after the fact.

positioning.basis: sum of disclosed net short positions at or above 0.5% of shares outstanding, as published by the national regulator

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Phase 1 median realised move was 2.81% (UK), 3.12% (DE), 4.19% (FR) against Japan's 2.87%, with the tail intact in all three -- 42%, 27% and 52% maxima and no price limit to truncate them.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read eu_priced_in.lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR borrowed from the US runs, none is measured on European data, and eu_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

anchor_coverage.basis: `anchor_covered` is true only where the national short register returned a disclosed net short position for THIS issuer. A name the register was read for and does not name reads 0.0 -- real, but the 0.5% truncation floor rather than a measurement, and below $1m/day of turnover 168 of 190 sampled UK issuers read exactly that. The turnover floor moved from $1m to $200k on 2026-09-19, so this field is how the cost of that move is made visible: eu_resolve.py reports the Spearman split by it, with the count in each arm.

anchor_quality.basis: magnitude: realised vol plus a reaction history, capped at 0.5 because neither is an option-implied move. direction: how many of the two positioning components resolved, capped at 0.45 because neither is 25-delta skew and Europe has no margin-balance component to add, and held to 0.15 where the register was read and does not name this issuer -- a truncated zero is not a disclosure.

evidence.text: The half-year about to be printed will show a Produit d'Activite Courante near EUR50m against EUR36.5m in H1 2025 (+39%) — roughly 72% of the ENTIRE unrevised full-year consensus of EUR69.75m delivered in six months — and the conversion arithmetic that the two covering analysts have not updated since 24 March 2026 is what the print actually tests.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the line that produced the two -8% prints in the baseline. 2026-03-24: FY2025 PAC of EUR59.7m matched only Kepler Cheuvreux's PESSIMISTIC EUR60m case against an optimistic EUR66m, net income EUR25.1m against Kepler's EUR27.8m and EPS EUR0.42 against EUR0.47 — the stock fell 8.19% on the day despite a simultaneously disclosed +40% activity pace. 2024-03-26 fell 8.34% on the same line. The three September half-year prints are much smaller: -0.51% (2023), +1.80% (2024), -1.51% (2025) — and the 2025 one fell even though net income doubled and ROE hit 20.3%. So this line can hurt badly in March and has never paid more than +1.80% in September.
evidence.why_not_priced: The +70% itself IS disclosed — it was filed as 'Informations privilegiees' on 2026-06-01 and carried in English and French — so I am NOT claiming an undisclosed fact, and researcher_europe/LESSONS.md is right that a pre-print privileged filing means most of the news is out. What is unpriced is the conversion and the fact that nothing has moved to reflect it. If the market had absorbed it, the two covering analysts would not still be carrying price targets 'last updated on Mar 24, 2026' (stockanalysis/S&P Global), the FY2026 revenue estimate would not still read EUR69.75m — which requires June-December 2026 to run at EUR3.92m/month, 21% BELOW the 2025 average and 54% below the disclosed Jan-May 2026 rate — and the stock would not be at EUR5.25 against EUR5.33 on the morning of the release, nearer its EUR4.87 52-week low than its EUR6.19 high, with a 20-day run-up of +1.74%. A French analyst wrote the same observation into a headline on 2026-09-03: 'nette acceleration de l'activite, mais le titre reste sans reaction'. Coverage is 2 analysts on $276k/day of turnover, the band where nobody is positioned for a confirmed fact. This size is already NET of the two things that break the conversion and broke the March print: approximately 45% of value created is redistributed to staff as variable compensation, and Momentum 2028 adds about EUR3m of incremental investment across full-year 2026 — ABC Bourse makes exactly this objection ('Cette phase de developpement pourrait temporairement limiter la conversion de la hausse d'activite en resultat net'). I have netted it here rather than carrying it as a second, contradictory finding.
evidence.independence: The consensus side and the activity side come from different documents. Activity: the issuer's own MAR filing, [url removed] (2026-06-01). Bar: [url removed] . Independent third read that the price has not responded: [url removed] (2026-09-03). Note this finding shares the 2026-06-01 release with finding 2 below; they use different sentences of it for different purposes (this one the quantum, that one the market-conditions sentence) and I have sized them so they do not double-count the same money.

evidence.text: The obvious bear read of the H2-to-date pace comment — index VIX at its 2026 low, therefore a repeat of the H2 2025 collapse that got the last September print sold — is probably keyed to the wrong market parameter: the company states the Jan-May surge happened in conditions 'broadly comparable' to the prior year, making it capability rather than weather, and H2 2026 has carried record single-stock dispersion with S&P 500 pairwise correlation in the bottom 1% since 2005.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the decisive line on this name in September. On 2025-09-23 the reported half was outstanding — net income doubled, ROE 20.3%, two EUR0.10 interims declared — and the stock fell 1.51%, because the release flagged that volatility had returned to historically low levels since June and H2 activity was down on H1. Kepler's later summary of that year confirms the mechanism: 'l'annee a ete marquee par un premier semestre tres solide, suivi de conditions de marche moins favorables au second semestre'. Conversely on 2026-03-24 a +40% pace statement was NOT enough to save a print whose P&L missed. So a constructive pace comment is necessary but not sufficient, and a weak one is close to sufficient for a negative day.
evidence.why_not_priced: The visible, quotable, terminal-level statistic on volatility is the VIX, and it is at its 2026 low — 14.2 on 2026-08-14 and 14.81 at the close on 2026-09-18, down from 21.51 in early June. Anyone previewing this print off the wire copy reaches for that number and reproduces the September-2025 trade. What the VIX does not describe is the environment a relative-value arbitrageur is actually paid in: on 2026-07-09 the Cboe S&P 500 Constituent Volatility Index closed at 49.98 against a VIX of 15.84, an all-time record 34.14-point gap and the 98th percentile for VIXEQ, and as of 2026-08-14 the average 60-day pairwise correlation among S&P 500 constituents sat in the bottom 1% of observations since 2005. Low index vol produced by low correlation and high single-stock vol is the opposite regime, for this business, from the genuinely quiet summer of 2025. If the market had made this distinction the stock would not be flat-to-down through a quarter in which its own disclosed activity pace accelerated from +40% (20 March) to +70% (end May). I am sizing this at less than half of finding 1 because LESSONS.md is explicit that macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company or a direct counterparty has said it, and no [THE COMPANY] document names dispersion; the company statement I quote covers January-May, not July-September.
evidence.independence: The dispersion and correlation series are from a source with no relationship to the company: [url removed] (2026-08-20). The 'capability not context' reading is reached independently by a French analyst who is not one of the two covering brokers: [url removed] (2026-09-03). Shares the 2026-06-01 filing with finding 1, on a different sentence.

evidence.text: The 22 September release is the scheduled venue for the first half-yearly distribution decision under the new semi-annual policy, where an already-announced EUR0.20 December interim has to be reconciled with an H1 EPS near EUR0.36-0.40 and a stated 66% payout ratio — against a consensus 2026 DPS of only EUR0.35 on a stock already yielding 6.5%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Distribution is the single most reliably price-moving line on this name, and it has cut both ways. The 2025-09-23 half-year release declared two EUR0.10 interims and the stock still fell 1.51%. The 2026-03-24 release cut the total 2025 distribution shape to EUR0.34 with an 81% payout and the stock fell 8.19%. In a EUR314m name held largely for a 6.3-6.5% yield, a distribution that merely meets what was already announced is worth nothing and one that lags is worth several points; the asymmetry here is that a raise has not been contemplated by the unrevised estimates.
evidence.why_not_priced: The EUR0.20 is public, so a bare confirmation is neutral and that is why this is the smallest of the three sizes. What is not in the estimates is the arithmetic that a half earning EUR0.36-0.40 per share makes EUR0.20 a ~52% half-year payout against a stated 66% policy, leaving visible headroom at the very moment the board first exercises the new semi-annual mechanism. If the market were carrying that, the 2026 DPS line in consensus would not still read EUR0.35 — barely above the EUR0.34 paid for 2025 — and the yield would not still be 6.48% on a name whose run-rate earnings are ~39% higher than the year that produced it. The offsetting risk, which is why the low end of my band is negative: the 2025 annual release also signalled an intention to strengthen equity via a dividend-reinvestment option from end-2026, and an income-oriented French retail base can read a scrip option as cash retention rather than as capital-return growth.
evidence.independence: The semi-annual switch and the EUR0.20 figure are independently reported by a second French outlet: [url removed] (2026-03-24). The policy floor and payout ratio are in the issuer's own English release, [url removed] . This finding rests on a different document from findings 1 and 2.

evidence.text: Price-target and estimate revisions from the two covering brokers (Kepler Cheuvreux, target EUR7.40, and TP ICAP Midcap, target EUR6.60) are both stale — Kepler's dates to 2026-03-24 and TP ICAP's to 2025-04-07 — and a half-year PAC near EUR50m makes an upward revision of the FY2026 EUR69.75m revenue and EUR0.52 EPS lines close to mechanical. Notes typically land in the days after the release, not in the single session this stage scores.

Payment of the first interim under the new semi-annual policy, EUR0.20 per share, scheduled for December 2026 — the amount may be confirmed or revised on 22 September but the cash and any scrip election resolve long after the window.

options.reason: No European single-stock option chain is retrievable from a free source. Yahoo returns 0 expiries and 0 contracts for .L, .DE and .PA symbols against 21 and 196 for AAPL on the same crumb; Eurex's daily reference file carries trading parameters but no settlement prices, no open interest and no underlying ISIN map, and its statistics page is JavaScript with no JSON endpoint. So there is no event-implied move and no skew, and this baseline supplies its own priced_lean_pct and anchor_quality from the national short registers instead. This holds for all ten markets; nothing measured in 2026-09 on …

consensus.basis: Sell-side coverage, carried because it is the measurable proxy for this stage's thesis. Phase 1 measured 1-2 analysts below $1m/day of turnover, 5-7 at $1-5m, 11-13 at $5-25m and 16-19 above, consistently across all three markets. eu_resolve.py ranks the hunt BY this band so the thesis is tested rather than selected on.

history.caveat: Dates are REAL: each row is a results announcement the market's own archive records on that date, and the move is over this stage's own window. Only the UK (Investegate) and Norway (Oslo NewsWeb) reach this state; the other eight markets are estimated.

event_plausibility.basis: vendor forward calendar (TradingView), measured at a 2.2% phantom rate on 90 UK rows against the RNS record. Confirmation against Investegate (RNS mirror) is eu_resolve.py's job, after the fact.

positioning.basis: sum of disclosed net short positions at or above 0.5% of shares outstanding, as published by the national regulator

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Phase 1 median realised move was 2.81% (UK), 3.12% (DE), 4.19% (FR) against Japan's 2.87%, with the tail intact in all three -- 42%, 27% and 52% maxima and no price limit to truncate them.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read eu_priced_in.lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR borrowed from the US runs, none is measured on European data, and eu_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

evidence.text: The -11.76% on 28 July was not a margin miss - margin ROSE to 11.1% from 11.0% - it was one unquantified paragraph: 'changes to the regulated mechanics of Demand Flexibility have begun to crystallise, and are expected to reduce recurring revenue per EV charger towards a more sustainable level early in the second half.' Demand Flexibility sits inside Energy Transition, which RBC sizes at ~11% of group sales but MORE THAN 20% of earnings, so the market de-rated ~20% of earnings on an unsized regulatory haircut. Tomorrow is the first disclosure with two months of post-change trading behind it, and the company has already twice said the change is 'consistent with the Board's expectations' while upgrading FY27 in the same announcement.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance upgrades at [THE COMPANY] have been paid: FY25 full-year TU 2026-01-29 +7.09%, FY25 results with the FY26 >GBP37m guide 2026-03-25 +8.40%, Q1 upgrade to >GBP40m 2026-05-19 +2.13%. The single exception is 2026-07-28, where an FY27 upgrade came attached to this new structural caveat and the stock fell 11.76%. Both prior interim results prints were positive: 2024-09-10 +2.35%, 2025-09-09 +9.46%. Across all 17 observed prints the mean is +2.53% and 10 of 17 are positive.
evidence.why_not_priced: The attribution is wrong in the coverage the marginal buyer reads. RTT News reported the fall with no explanation at all ('the article offers no analysis or commentary about the reason behind the share price drop'); MarketBeat's instant alert attributed it to 'the modest margin improvement... appears to have disappointed investors', which is factually backwards since the margin rose 10bp and the company said so in the same bullet. If the market had the right model of what tomorrow resolves, you would not see five analysts all constructive (RBC Buy 320p, Deutsche Bank upgrading to Buy 270p on 8 September explicitly to preview this print, average target 289p) while the stock sits 8% below its pre-update level - you would see targets cut to reflect a sized haircut. Nobody has sized it publicly because the company has not yet given the number.
evidence.independence: The Q1 2026 trading update of 19 May 2026 contains no mention of any regulatory change and instead says 'Demand Flexibility revenues from EV chargers increased significantly during the quarter', confirming the 28 July paragraph was genuinely new information rather than a restatement - [url removed]

evidence.text: The one P&L line NOT pre-announced is adjusted PBT / adjusted EPS, and it should show a step change in optics. In H1 2025 adjusted operating profit rose 9.5% but adjusted PBT FELL 3.6% and adjusted EPS rose only 3.5%, because bank net debt had ballooned 72.6% YoY (GBP39.4m to GBP68.0m) on acquisitions and the interest charge was ~GBP3.0m. In H1 2026 net debt is flat YoY at GBP69.6m against GBP68.0m, so that step-up has annualised and UK rates have fallen. On a flat ~GBP3.0-3.1m finance charge, c.GBP15.8m of adjusted operating profit implies adjusted PBT of ~GBP12.7m (+17.6%) and adjusted EPS of ~6.8p (+15%) against last year's +3.5% - the earnings line growing FASTER than the pre-announced operating line, which is the reverse of last year.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025 interims printed adjusted EPS +3.5% against adjusted operating profit +9.5% - the weakest EPS/EBIT gap in the record - and the stock still rose 9.46%, so this shareholder base is not punitive on the EPS line. There is no instance in the 17-event record of the EPS line itself being the stated driver of a move.
evidence.why_not_priced: Every piece of wire copy and every broker summary I found quotes the pre-announced operating profit ('+14%') and none carries a PBT or EPS figure, because the trading update does not give one. The market's anchor for this print is therefore an EBIT number; the EPS number is the one that lands tomorrow and it is arithmetically better than the anchor. If this were priced you would see previews quoting an H1 EPS estimate - Deutsche Bank's 8 September preview, as reported, quotes revenue and divisional growth only. My PBT/EPS figures are MY estimate from two primary documents, clearly labelled, not a company number.
evidence.independence: Corroborated by the FY25 results RNS, which shows the same mechanism reversing over a full year once the debt annualised: adjusted operating profit +16.6% but adjusted EPS +20.0% - [url removed]

evidence.text: The entire disclosed short is one holder - Saba Capital Management, L.P. - at 0.80% of shares outstanding, which is ~1.21m shares against a September median daily volume of ~226k shares, i.e. roughly five sessions of volume to cover. Saba peaked at 1.02% on 2026-02-18, covered to 0.59% by 2026-06-19, then rebuilt to 0.80% by 28 August across the July de-rating.

That caps how much squeeze fuel 0.80% represents.
evidence.why_not_priced: The aggregated register the market reads publishes one number per issuer with no holder name and no history, so '0.8%' is all a screen shows. The per-holder file back to 2012 is a separate FCA document that resolves it to a single identified holder and a two-year trajectory. That said, I am sizing this small precisely because 0.80% is not a crowded short - if it were the 18-23% of float that produced 20%+ squeezes in the US record, this would be the largest finding here and it is not.

evidence.text: The FY26 guide of >GBP40m requires H2 adjusted operating profit of at least GBP24.2m against GBP20.0m in H2 2025 - +21% YoY, ACCELERATING from the +14.5% just delivered in H1 - and it has to be delivered in the very half the Demand Flexibility revenue-per-charger haircut lands in. In the same half, H1 drop-through was poor: my decomposition of the disclosed 'c.120%' Energy Transition growth and 'c.6%' core growth puts Energy Transition revenue at ~GBP18.2m from ~GBP8.3m, i.e. ~GBP9.9m of incremental revenue in a supposedly high-margin stream, for only GBP2.0m of incremental group profit and 10bp of margin.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The only time an H2-weighting question was live at a [THE COMPANY] print was the 2025 interims, where the company said 'firmly on track to deliver full year expectations with a strong order book entering H2' and the stock rose 9.46% - the market took the reassurance rather than doing the arithmetic. H2 weighting is also normal here: H2 was 59% of FY25 operating profit and 57% of FY24, against the 60.5% FY26 implies, so this is a stretch and not an outlier.
evidence.why_not_priced: The H2 bridge needs two documents that are six months apart - the FY25 results for the GBP33.8m full-year and GBP13.8m H1 comparator, and the July update for the GBP15.8m and the >GBP40m guide - and no piece of coverage I found subtracts them. But I am sizing this SMALL and not large for two reasons the lessons file names: it agrees with a short seller who is already building, so it is likely in the price; and the revenue decomposition rests on two rounded percentages ('c.120%', 'c.6%') and is fragile to a point either way.
evidence.independence: The same RNS supplies the inventory build that CORROBORATES rather than contradicts the ramp - 'Bank Net Debt... increased slightly to GBP69.6m... reflecting an investment in inventory ahead of the second half' - so the company has put stock behind the H2 it is guiding to. Shares a document with the net-debt finding below; see that finding's independence note. [url removed]

evidence.text: Dr Thorsten Muller became CEO on 1 September 2026, three weeks before this print, succeeding founder John Hornby after 21 years. He did not set the FY26 >GBP40m or the FY27 'ahead of consensus' guidance - both were given on 28 July while Hornby was on sabbatical and while the board was still 'in advanced discussions with a number of candidates'. This is his first results statement and the first opportunity to rebase numbers he does not own.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent on this name - Hornby ran it for the whole 17-event record, so there is no observation of how this shareholder base reacts to a CEO transition here. The CEO Retirement RNS (2026-06-15) and the Appointment RNS (2026-08-10) were both non-events for the tape: the stock closed 225p on 10 August against 226p on 7 August. That the appointment itself was a non-event is why the first-results risk is still live rather than already discharged.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a known fact with an unknown consequence, and the sell-side has priced the fact and not the consequence - Deutsche Bank upgraded to Buy on 8 September, a week after Muller started, on divisional growth forecasts that assume the inherited guidance holds. If the market were pricing reset risk you would expect the shares to have drifted DOWN into a new CEO's first print rather than up 9.3% in five sessions. I hold this as a fat left tail rather than a central case: three weeks is too short to kitchen-sink a half that was already pre-announced under the previous regime, and a strategic reset at a UK small cap normally waits for full-year results or a capital markets day.
evidence.independence: The departing founder-CEO sold 505,000 shares at 224.06p (~GBP1.13m) on 21 August 2026, two days before the 30-day closed period for a 22 September interim announcement would have begun - a timing detail visible only in the RNS, which points the same way on incentives - [url removed]

evidence.text: Bank net debt rose GBP17.3m in the half - from GBP52.3m at 31 December 2025 to GBP69.6m at 30 June 2026 - against a GBP0.6m FALL over the equivalent half of 2025. The 28 July RNS framed it only against the prior-year half-end ('increased slightly to GBP69.6m (H1 2025: GBP68.0m)'), which is the comparison that makes a GBP17.3m six-month build read as GBP1.6m. Tomorrow's cash flow statement and net debt bridge make it explicit, and adjusted free cash flow should land roughly GBP10m+ worse than the GBP10.3m of H1 2025.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Decisive, and it is why this is [sizing note removed].4 and not -1.5: at the 2025 interims bank net debt printed +72.6% YoY (GBP39.4m to GBP68.0m) and the stock rose 9.46% on the day. This shareholder base has demonstrably looked straight through a far larger balance-sheet expansion at this exact event. The FY24-to-FY25 pattern also shows the working capital reversing - adjusted free cash flow GBP3.5m in 2024 then GBP30.4m in 2025.
evidence.why_not_priced: Every summary of the July update I read - the AI abstract on Investegate, the Kalkine and Financial-News write-ups, the [url removed] piece - repeats the company's own YoY framing and none compares the GBP69.6m to the GBP52.3m the company itself published in March. But the lessons file is explicit that financing is a question, not a verdict, and the answer here is benign: the company says the money bought 'an investment in inventory ahead of the second half', and the H2 the guidance requires is exactly the ramp that inventory would serve. So this is an optic on the day, not a solvency point - leverage still fell to 1.5x, inside the 1-2x target range.
evidence.independence: Shares the 28 July RNS with the H2-ramp finding above; the GBP52.3m comparator comes from a different document (the FY25 results RNS, 2026-03-25). The two findings are NOT independent of each other and point opposite ways on the same inventory build - the H2-ramp finding treats it as an unmet requirement, this one treats it as a cash cost, and the inventory itself is the reason both are sized small.

evidence.text: The stock closed 235.0p on 21 September, up 4.91% on the day against the FTSE 250's +1.18%, on 414,767 shares versus a September median of ~226k - roughly 3.7 points of idiosyncratic move on 1.8x normal volume, the session before a print, with no RNS from the company since 24 August. Over five sessions it is +9.3% (215p on 14 September). Anticipatory buying, at least partly domestic retail: SQC Research published a buy note on 17 September at 220p with a 275p target saying the results 'will be good and could show that the next year will be better than market expectations'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is why the penalty is only -0.4. Measured on [THE COMPANY]'s own 17 prints, the 5-day run-up into the event has NO predictive power for the reaction: Spearman +0.096, and the five events with a >3% run-up averaged +4.43% against +1.75% for the other twelve - i.e. on this name a run-up has historically preceded BETTER prints, not worse. The one cautionary precedent is 2024-01-30, the largest run-up in the sample at +9.70%, which printed -4.76%. The current +9.3% is the second-largest.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is not 'unpriced' - it IS the price, and I am carrying it as a debit against the other findings rather than as information. What it tells me is that some of the relief trade in finding 1 has already been taken, which is exactly what should be visible if my central thesis were becoming consensus. I looked for a company-specific cause for the 21 September move and found none: the Investegate RNS history shows nothing since the 24 August PDMR notification, and the Deutsche Bank upgrade that plausibly caused the 8 September +4.0% is two weeks old and was fully retraced by 14 September.
evidence.independence: The FTSE 250 comparison is a second, independent series - [url removed] - and confirms the move is idiosyncratic rather than market beta.

history.caveat: Dates are REAL: each row is a results announcement the market's own archive records on that date, and the move is over this stage's own window. Only the UK (Investegate) and Norway (Oslo NewsWeb) reach this state; the other eight markets are estimated.

event_plausibility.basis: vendor forward calendar (TradingView), measured at a 2.2% phantom rate on 90 UK rows against the RNS record. Confirmation against Investegate (RNS mirror) is eu_resolve.py's job, after the fact.

positioning.basis: sum of disclosed net short positions at or above 0.5% of shares outstanding, as published by the national regulator

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Phase 1 median realised move was 2.81% (UK), 3.12% (DE), 4.19% (FR) against Japan's 2.87%, with the tail intact in all three -- 42%, 27% and 52% maxima and no price limit to truncate them.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read eu_priced_in.lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR borrowed from the US runs, none is measured on European data, and eu_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

anchor_coverage.basis: `anchor_covered` is true only where the national short register returned a disclosed net short position for THIS issuer. A name the register was read for and does not name reads 0.0 -- real, but the 0.5% truncation floor rather than a measurement, and below $1m/day of turnover 168 of 190 sampled UK issuers read exactly that. The turnover floor moved from $1m to $200k on 2026-09-19, so this field is how the cost of that move is made visible: eu_resolve.py reports the Spearman split by it, with the count in each arm.

anchor_quality.basis: magnitude: realised vol plus a reaction history, capped at 0.5 because neither is an option-implied move. direction: how many of the two positioning components resolved, capped at 0.45 because neither is 25-delta skew and Europe has no margin-balance component to add, and held to 0.15 where the register was read and does not name this issuer -- a truncated zero is not a disclosure.

evidence.text: The interim dividend is set by formula at one third of ~50% of expected full-year adjusted post-tax profit, and FY26 guidance of ~£38.0m is still ~5% profit growth on 2025 — so the arithmetic points to an interim DPS of roughly 7.5-7.8p against 7.2p last year, an increase, at a moment when the default retail read after a 20% profit warning is a cut.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last time MAB moved this line it was the February 2025 policy reset that took FY DPS from 28.2p to 22.5p — a cut of ~20% — and the stock still rose 8.12% on the 2026-03-17 Final Results that confirmed it and promised a progressive policy. The line has not been a source of downside on this name; the two prior Interim Results prints that carried a dividend declaration moved +13.24% and +7.94%.
evidence.why_not_priced: If it were priced the stock would not be trading at 382.5p against an implied ~23p full-year DPS — a 6.1% yield on a business with 0.1x leverage, £3.3m net debt, 121% adjusted cash conversion and £56.7m of regulatory-capital headroom. Three analysts cover the name (baseline consensus.analyst_count = 3) and the two sell-side aggregators reachable here still carry price targets of 975p-1250p against a 382.5p spot, i.e. nobody has republished a post-warning model in public. The marginal holder of a £222m Main Market name with three analysts is domestic retail and adviser money that reads the dividend line first, and the run-up (-26.16% over 20 days) is the shape of a market that has priced a cut, not an increase.
evidence.independence: Corroborated by a different document: the 2025 interims set the precedent that the interim payment is one third of the expected full-year dividend (7.2p of 22.5p) and describe it as 'in line with the new capital allocation framework and dividend policy announced in February 2025' — https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/mortgage-advice-bureau-holdings---mab1/interim-results/9124509 (2025-09-23). evidence.text: [THE COMPANY] contractually committed, in its own communique, to give a status update on the strategic review of its Lockers business ON THIS RELEASE (23 September 2026) -- with Rothschild & Co, Societe Generale and Darrois Villey already mandated at launch -- and only part of the deal option is still in the price: the stock rose +6.00% on the 20 July announcement and peaked at EUR 13.68 on 3 August (+14.0% vs EUR 12.00 pre-announcement) but sits at EUR 12.46 today, so roughly two thirds of the peak premium has bled out ahead of the one date the company itself named.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is exactly one prior instance of this line and it is the launch itself: 2026-07-20, the stock closed +6.00% at EUR 12.72 on 96,222 shares against a 60-day median of 37,606 (2.6x), then drifted to EUR 13.68 by 3 August. The line has never been tested by an UPDATE, which is why my band is wide in both directions: the modal outcome is 'process continues, no decision', a signed or near-signed disposal is the fat right tail, and 'we will retain and invest' is the left tail. The path to the equity is stated rather than assumed: net debt was EUR 682m at 31 January 2026 at 3.0x leverage including leasing (1.6x excluding), against a EUR 429m market capitalisation on 34,468,912 shares, so a disposal near the EUR 180m French estimate cuts net debt by about a quarter and removes the balance-sheet overhang that French coverage names as the single biggest concern on the name.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is partly priced and I size it as such -- the launch is English wire copy and the stock paid +6% for it. What is not in the price is the dated update. If the market were positioned for an outcome on 23 September, the stock would not have given back two thirds of its announcement premium into the one date the company named, and the 5-day run-up would not be +0.48% with the 20-day at -3.11%; a market anticipating a disposal announcement bids a EUR 429m equity ahead of a EUR 180m asset decision rather than drifting from EUR 13.40 on 4 September to EUR 12.26 on 18 September. The AMF short register does not name the issuer, so there is no crowded short being squeezed and no positioning tell either way. With 5 analysts covering a name trading $0.5m a day, there is also no preview machine to put a probability-weighted disposal into the price the way there would be at 16-19 analysts.
evidence.independence: Two independent corroborations. (1) Sector context from a different publisher: Axios Pro reported the same day that the review 'follows FedEx and Advent's $9.2 billion bid for European locker firm InPost', i.e. the European locker sector has an active strategic bidder -- [url removed] (2026-07-20). (2) An independent French sizing of the asset, DR Bourse 2026-07-21: 'Sur une valorisation de 15x l'EBITDA, l'activite Lockers pourrait etre cedee pour 180 M EUR' [At a 15x EBITDA valuation, the Lockers business could be sold for EUR 180m] -- [url removed] . EUR 180m is 42% of the EUR 429m market capitalisation. NOTE THE DEPENDENCE WITH FINDING 4: finding 4 is a haircut on this finding's upside (the asset is trading worse than the sale narrative), not an independent negative, and this finding is sized well below the full option value partly for that reason.

evidence.text: [THE COMPANY] voluntarily pre-disclosed a strongly positive operational datapoint about the quarter being reported -- Digital global bookings up more than 20% year on year like-for-like in Q2, with French e-invoicing bookings up more than ten-fold -- four weeks before the print and before the quiet period opened, which materially lowers the probability of the FY2026 guidance cut that is this stock's only demonstrated -15% trigger.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line is the whole reaction function on this name and it is cleanly measured over three events. FY2025 guidance CUT at the H1 2025 print (filed 2025-09-24 after the close; 'FY 2025 revenue is now expected to decline by a low single digit on an organic basis', replacing 'acceleration in organic revenue growth') -> EUR 15.94 to EUR 13.10, -17.82%. FY2025 results with a EUR 124m Mail goodwill impairment (filed 2026-03-25 after the close) -> EUR 12.68 to EUR 10.88, -14.20%. FY2026 guidance CONFIRMED at Q1 (filed 2026-05-21 after the close) -> EUR 11.98 to EUR 12.34, +3.01%. So this stock pays roughly +3% for a confirmation and roughly -15% for a cut: sharply asymmetric, and the asymmetry is the reason my emitted move is far below the upside of my band.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is partially priced -- the stock rose +3.26% on 92,795 shares (2.5x the 60-day median) on 24 August -- and then the whole of that move was given back: EUR 13.18 on 31 August to EUR 12.46 today, -5.5%. So the market bought the datapoint and then sold the print risk. What is NOT priced is its function as a negative signal about a guidance cut: managements four weeks from cutting a full-year guide do not usually publish '+20% bookings growth' under their own name. If the market had read it that way, the pre-print drift would not have been -8.5% from EUR 13.40 on 4 September to EUR 12.26 on 18 September. The French-language version of the same release exists in the AMF flux, so this is not a language gap -- it is an attention gap on a 5-analyst name, and the release was categorised 001006 (ordinary communique), not as regulated results information, which is exactly the classification that defeats a headline filter.
evidence.independence: Corroborated by a different document and a different metric: the Q1 2026 release reports Digital annual recurring revenue of EUR 257m at end-Q1, +15.9% annualised organic -- [url removed] (2026-05-21). And independently, the structural driver went live inside the reporting gap: [THE COMPANY] filed on 2026-09-01 that it and its partners 'Support More Than 800,000 Entities as France's First Phase of E-Invoicing Reform Takes Effect', with Serensia by [THE COMPANY] definitively approved by the DGFiP -- AMF flux record, PDF at [url removed] (2026-09-01). Note the shared-document caveat with finding 4: both touch the 21 May Q1 release, but this finding's load is carried by the 24 August document.

evidence.text: The AMF published a 'franchissement de seuils' on [THE COMPANY] on 21 September 2026 -- two days before the print, in French only, with no English wire version -- whose headline (a holder crossing DOWN through 5%) reads far more negative than the arithmetic inside it: Janus Henderson Investors UK sold only 32,062 shares, 1.8% of its holding, and still holds 1,709,808 shares or 4.96%, having crossed UP through 5% on 23 July by buying on market three sessions after the Lockers review was announced.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measurable on this name: the AMF short register has never named [THE COMPANY] (anchor_covered false, register_read_no_position), so there is no disclosed-short history to read a squeeze or a cover off, and threshold declarations on a EUR 429m small cap do not normally carry a same-week price signature. I size it small for exactly that reason. Its value here is that it is the ONLY positioning anchor this name has, because the baseline's priced_lean_pct is 100% the run-up term.
evidence.why_not_priced: It exists only in the AMF's French declaration archive and in no English wire, no broker note and no aggregator I could reach. If the market had read it, a 'largest disclosed holder cuts below 5% two days before results' headline on a EUR 429m name would have shown up as a down day on elevated volume on 21 or 22 September; instead the stock traded +1.14% on 50,186 shares and +0.48% on 14,420 shares, the latter being 38% of the 60-day median volume -- the two quietest sessions of the month. The 1.8% trim is also far too small to explain the one genuinely anomalous tape event in the window (553,716 shares on 18 September, 14.7x the median, at -1.13%), which I could not attribute and therefore score at zero.
evidence.independence: The two paired declarations are separate AMF filings by the same declarant and I am treating them as ONE finding, not two. Independent corroboration of the direction of travel from a different source family: the AMF flux carries no information privilegiee / communique ad hoc from [THE COMPANY] between the 9 September quiet-period start and 22 September -- the only filings in that span are these two declarations and a 14 September marketing release -- [url removed] . Nothing is pre-released, so no holder is trading on a leaked number.

evidence.text: The asset being put up for review is trading badly on the line a buyer pays for: [THE COMPANY]'s own Q1 2026 release discloses that Lockers non-recurring revenue fell 44.6% organically, taking the whole Lockers segment to -3.8% organic after +11.2% in H1 2025, and French coverage explicitly names this as the concern hanging over the 23 September checkpoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The market has already been shown this exact number once and looked straight through it: the -44.6% was disclosed in the 21 May 2026 Q1 release and the stock rose +3.01% the next session, because subscription revenue in the same segment grew 18% organically and is now 80% of Lockers revenue against two thirds in FY2025. That is the single strongest argument for sizing this small, and it is why I cut it rather than carrying it at a full point. Its live bite is narrower: the FY2026 guide contains an explicit 'EBITDA margin above 10% in Lockers' target, up from 5.0% in FY2025, and a second weak hardware quarter puts that specific line at risk on a name that pays roughly -15% for a guidance cut.
evidence.why_not_priced: The number itself IS priced -- it was in the May release and the stock went up. What the French commentary adds, and the English coverage does not, is the link between the hardware collapse and the sale process: English Q1 coverage described it only as 'hardware sales were impacted by high comparison base', which is a comp story, while the French note frames it as the reason the 23 September checkpoint is a risk rather than a catalyst. I have deliberately NOT sized that reframing as new information about the quarter; I have sized it as a haircut on finding 1. If the market had already applied that haircut, the stock would not still be carrying +3.8% of the July announcement premium.
evidence.independence: The -44.6% is confirmed in the primary company document, which is what makes it usable at all rather than a secondary claim: 'Lockers revenue amounted to EUR 24 million in first-quarter 2026, down 3.8% on an organic basis', with non-recurring revenue down 44.6% organically and subscription-related revenue up 18% -- [url removed] (2026-05-21). NOT INDEPENDENT OF FINDING 1: this is the offsetting side of the same asset and I have netted it rather than counting it twice -- finding 1 is [sizing note removed].5 against a French estimate of EUR 180m (42% of market cap) precisely because this exists.

evidence.text: The actual announcement, signing or completion of a Lockers transaction, as opposed to a status update. The company itself refuses to date it: 'sans aucune certitude quant a l'issue, a la structure ou au calendrier d'une eventuelle operation' [with no certainty as to the outcome, the structure or the timing of any possible transaction]. If it lands after 24 September it is worth nothing to this ranking, and on a EUR 180m estimate against a EUR 429m market cap it is where most of the value of this situation sits.

Q3 2026 revenue, 1 December 2026 after the close, which is the first release that will carry any revenue from the French e-invoicing mandate: the mandate went live 1 September 2026, which is the start of [THE COMPANY]'s Q3 (fiscal year ends 31 January), so the H1 period being reported on 23 September ended 31 July and contains none of it.

Les Echos, Investir, [url removed] Zonebourse and actusnews: not retried, per the measured 403-to-both-tools finding. I routed around them and note that Boursorama republishes Zonebourse wire copy, which is how I recovered the French communique body at [url removed] (HTTP 200).

No named bidder, no reported approach and no leak on the Lockers process in any French or English source since the 20 July launch. Searched in both languages including specific counterparties (InPost, Mondial Relay, Vinted Go). CEP Research's 22 July piece is paywalled to the first paragraph.

No information privilegiee / communique ad hoc from [THE COMPANY] in the AMF regulated-information flux between the 9 September quiet-period start and 22 September. The only filings in that span are the two threshold declarations of 21 September and a 14 September analyst-award marketing release. So nothing about H1 has been pre-released -- this is a negative result that raises my magnitude rather than lowering it.

Could not attribute the one genuinely anomalous tape event: 553,716 shares on 2026-09-18, 14.7x the 60-day median of 37,606, at -1.13%. It is NOT the Euronext CAC-family September annual review -- [THE COMPANY] appears in none of the additions or removals for SBF 120, CAC Mid 60, CAC Small or CAC All-Tradable, effective 21 September ([url removed] -- and no AMF declaration corresponds to it. A comparable 1,264,857-share day on 2026-05-29 suggests a recurring index weight/free-float rebalance rather than information. Unattributed, therefore scored at 0.

No sourceable H1 2026 or FY2026 consensus for revenue or EBIT from two agreeing places. A single French aggregator snippet gave ~EUR 1.12bn FY2026 revenue, which cannot be reconciled with a -2%/+2% organic guide on a FY2025 base of EUR 1,036m plus a EUR 12m-per-quarter FX headwind, so I discarded it. My bar is the company's own guidance instead, which is why no finding is sized off a consensus miss.
No plan social, restructuring, site closure or employment news at [THE COMPANY] in the French national or regional press for 2026.

AMF positions courtes nettes: [THE COMPANY] is absent from the register as of 2026-09-21. A truncated zero at the 0.5% threshold, not a measurement -- no short-interest finding is possible on this name.

No analyst rating change, downgrade or price-target cut published in the quiet period (9-22 September) that I could find in either language. Standing sell-side is stale and far above spot: consensus target EUR 19.40-20.00 against EUR 12.46.

history.caveat: Dates are REAL: each row is a results announcement the market's own archive records on that date, and the move is over this stage's own window. Only the UK (Investegate) and Norway (Oslo NewsWeb) reach this state; the other eight markets are estimated.

event_plausibility.basis: vendor forward calendar (TradingView), measured at a 2.2% phantom rate on 90 UK rows against the RNS record. Confirmation against Investegate (RNS mirror) is eu_resolve.py's job, after the fact.

positioning.basis: sum of disclosed net short positions at or above 0.5% of shares outstanding, as published by the national regulator

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Phase 1 median realised move was 2.81% (UK), 3.12% (DE), 4.19% (FR) against Japan's 2.87%, with the tail intact in all three -- 42%, 27% and 52% maxima and no price limit to truncate them.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read eu_priced_in.lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR borrowed from the US runs, none is measured on European data, and eu_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

anchor_coverage.basis: `anchor_covered` is true only where the national short register returned a disclosed net short position for THIS issuer. A name the register was read for and does not name reads 0.0 -- real, but the 0.5% truncation floor rather than a measurement, and below $1m/day of turnover 168 of 190 sampled UK issuers read exactly that. The turnover floor moved from $1m to $200k on 2026-09-19, so this field is how the cost of that move is made visible: eu_resolve.py reports the Spearman split by it, with the count in each arm.

anchor_quality.basis: magnitude: realised vol plus a reaction history, capped at 0.5 because neither is an option-implied move. direction: how many of the two positioning components resolved, capped at 0.45 because neither is 25-delta skew and Europe has no margin-balance component to add, and held to 0.15 where the register was read and does not name this issuer -- a truncated zero is not a disclosure.

first_hunter_context.bar: Ceres' own analyst-compiled consensus page, eight analysts, 'Consensus values updated as of 24 April 2026': FY2026e revenue GBP60.0m, gross profit GBP42.1m, Adj. EBITDA +GBP1.0m, EBIT -GBP11.4m, cash and short-term investments GBP74.8m. https://www.ceres.tech/investors/analyst-centre/consensus/ . Against it the company's own 26 March 2026 statement: 'Current contracted group revenue for 2026 is approximately GBP45m before any new business.' Note the page is four months stale and predates the June capital raise, so the GBP74.8m cash line is c.GBP100m too low by construction.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Disclosed aggregate net short 13.3% of shares outstanding at position date 18/09/2026 on the FCA aggregated register fetched 2026-09-22 (the baseline sealed 13.21% at 16/09), i.e. STILL BUILDING, and building through an 11% rally off the 15 September low. That is the 5th largest disclosed short in the whole 423-issuer UK register, behind only Vistry 16.76, Ibstock 16.32, Capita 13.41 and WH Smith 13.31. https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv . The per-holder file is a frozen snapshot -- its only sheet is titled 'Historic Disclosures 10.07.2026' and Ceres' last per-holder row is 09/07/2026 -- where the live names summed to roughly 6.6% (Marshall Wace 1.34, Arrowstreet 0.93, D. E. Shaw 0.70, Voleon 0.69, Systematica 0.60, Winton 0.50, Squarepoint 0.47, ActusRay 0.48, Walleye 0.47, CFM 0.46). So the position has roughly doubled since July and the identity of the marginal seller is not public. https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/data/short-positions-daily-update.xlsx
first_hunter_context.session_check: bmo, settled rather than defaulted. The issuer's own RNS 'Notice of Interim Results' (Investegate, 03 Sep 2026 07:00) states results for the six months ended 30 June 2026 will be announced on Wednesday, 23 September 2026, with a live Investor Meet Company presentation at 09:30 BST -- a 09:30 presentation implies a pre-open RNS, and every prior Ceres results RNS on the Investegate company archive is stamped 07:00 (Interim Results 26 Sep 2025 07:00; Final results 26 Mar 2026 07:00). https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/ceres-power-holdings--cwr/notice-of-interim-results/9752895

evidence.text: The bar Ceres itself publishes -- eight analysts, FY2026e revenue GBP60.0m and Adj. EBITDA of POSITIVE GBP1.0m -- sits GBP15m above the 'approximately GBP45m' of contracted 2026 revenue the company stated on 26 March 2026, and in the six months since Ceres has announced no new manufacturing-licence partner at all (the last was Weichai, 5 November 2025); the Centrica and Delta/Centrica partnerships of 26 March and 30 April 2026 disclose no licence fee, no revenue value and no recognition timing.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ceres is punished hard when the revenue outlook is trimmed: Trading update 24 Jan 2024 -15.10%, Final results 21 Mar 2025 -7.97%, and the last interims on 26 Sep 2025, at which FY2025 revenue was guided to 'around GBP32 million', -8.77%. All three are observed_rns rows in the sealed baseline. The one large positive results reaction, +26.57% on 27 Sep 2024, came in a half where a signed licence (Delta, GBP43m staged) was already funding the number.
evidence.why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced, and I have sized it accordingly. If it were fully priced the sell-side targets would not still be 920p (Jefferies, 10 June 2026) and 980p (Berenberg, May 2026) against a 415p spot, and the company would not still be publishing a breakeven-EBITDA 2026 on its own website five months after the contracted figure was set GBP15m lower. What IS priced is the direction -- a 13.3% short base is paid to hold exactly this view -- which is why this is -2.5 and not -6.
evidence.independence: Simply Wall St's read of the same post-FY25 revision, eight analysts cutting FY2026 revenue from GBP63.6m to GBP60.0m while raising the loss per share to GBP0.066: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/analysts-lowered-expectations-ceres-power-130138399.html

evidence.text: Ceres told the market in the Weichai licence RNS that the licence fees land in FY2026, on terms 'consistent with previous Ceres manufacturing licensing agreements' -- and the previous one, Delta Electronics in January 2024, was GBP43m staged with about half recognised in year one. Weichai then launched its CE-certified, Ceres-based SOFC system on 18 February 2026 with over 30,000 hours of cumulative operation, so the technology-transfer milestones that trigger those fees are running. That makes H1 2026 revenue likely to be UP against H1 2025's GBP21.1m, into a domestic narrative ('falling revenue', 'two fundraisings') and a short thesis that both assume the opposite.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The half in which the previous manufacturing licence fee was recognised was H1 2024: revenue GBP28.5m against GBP12-13m the year before, and the 27 Sep 2024 interims moved +26.57%, the largest reaction in the twelve observed_rns rows in the baseline. The mirror case is H1 2025, the half with no new licence: revenue fell 26% to GBP21.1m and the print moved -8.77%. This line has the widest realised dispersion of any at this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: The sentence is one clause in a thirteen-month-old RNS and it never reached the wire copy: the English-language coverage of Ceres in 2026 is about the AI-datacentre narrative, the June placing and the 50% drawdown, and the domestic retail write-ups (ABC Money, 30 July 2026) frame the name as 'falling revenue' full stop. If the market held the licence-phasing point, a name whose contracted 2026 revenue is 38% above its 2025 actual would not be trading 27% below its own June placing price with the disclosed short doubling. Note this does NOT lift FY2026 to the GBP60m bar -- Weichai is already inside the GBP45m contracted -- which is why it coexists with the finding above rather than contradicting it.
evidence.independence: Weichai's CE-certification launch of the Ceres-based system, 18 February 2026, is the physical milestone behind the fee, reported independently of Ceres: https://www.ceres.tech/newsroom/news-and-insights/ceres-partner-weichai-launches-stationary-power-sofc-system-at-ceremony-to-mark-its-ce-certification-with-tuev-sued/

evidence.text: Ceres disclosed in the 9 June 2026 placing RNS that it held 'unaudited cash and short-term investments of GBP78.7 million as of 31 May 2026' against GBP83.3m at 31 December 2025 -- an outflow of only GBP4.6m in five months, roughly half the FY2025 run-rate (net cash used in operating activities GBP20.1m; adjusted EBITDA loss GBP32.5m) -- and then raised GBP103m gross at 570p. So the 30 June 2026 balance sheet should carry roughly GBP175m of net cash and investments, about 20% of the GBP890m market capitalisation and about GBP100m above the FY2026e cash figure the company's own consensus page still shows.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Financing news at this name has been read both ways: the placing itself was met with a rise on admission (12 June 2026) because insiders subscribed and the CEO retained his shares, but the stock then fell from 570p to 362p by 1 September as the domestic press rolled the raise into a dilution-and-burn story. The FY2025 results on 26 Mar 2026 led with GBP83.3m of cash and a reduced outflow and moved +6.67%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Financing is a question here and the answer is a ramp, not distress: the money buys IP and a component supply facility, and three independent counterparties corroborate the ramp -- Delta is building at Tainan for production start by end-2026, Weichai has a CE-certified system, and Doosan signed a KRW108.7bn (c.GBP60m) SOFC stack export order with Reverion on 6 August 2026. The domestic read is the opposite: ABC Money on 30 July 2026 wrote that 'a further fundraising ... cannot be ruled out'. The arithmetic -- GBP4.6m of burn in five months -- was never in a headline; it sat in the ninth paragraph of a placing announcement that the market read for the price and the discount.
evidence.independence: The FY2025 results give the other half of the subtraction, 'Net cash and investments 83,272' and 'Net cash used in operating activities (20,070)': https://www.ceres.tech/media/jpmpucda/ceres-power-holdings-plc-final-results-statement-2026-march-26.pdf . The Doosan/Reverion order that corroborates the ramp: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/ceres-power-holdings--cwr/doosan-fuel-cell-sofc-order-with-reverion-gmbh/9708112

evidence.text: Ceres is the fifth most heavily shorted stock in the entire UK disclosed register -- 13.3% of shares outstanding at position date 18/09/2026, out of 423 issuers -- and the position was still being added to through an 11% rally (13.21% at 16/09 in the sealed baseline, 13.3% at 18/09 on the file fetched 2026-09-22). On 214.5m shares (BlackRock's TR-1 of 28 July 2026 pins 12,548,472 shares at 5.85%) that is 28.5m shares short against a 20-day median volume of 1.64m, or 17.4 days to cover, into a one-session event on a name with 79% 20-day realised volatility and no daily price limit.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline's twelve observed reactions have a median absolute move of 6.06% and a maximum of +26.57%, and the sealed lean already carries +3.0 for squeeze against -2.0 for building. What the lean cannot carry is the cover ratio: at 17.4 days the marginal short cannot exit into a 07:00 RNS, which is the mechanism behind the two US names in this repo's record that squeezed more than 20% from 18% and 23% of float.
evidence.why_not_priced: The level is in the baseline; the three things that are not are (a) the rank -- fifth of 423, which no summary of this name states, (b) the cover ratio of 17.4 sessions, which needs the share count out of a TR-1 and the volume out of the tape, and (c) that the FCA's per-holder file is frozen at 'Historic Disclosures 10.07.2026', where these same holders summed to roughly 6.6%, so the doubling since July is invisible at holder level and nobody can see who is short. If the squeeze risk were priced, the December 2025 Grizzly short report would not still be the top organic search result for this company's commercial prospects while the sell-side sits at 920-980p.
evidence.independence: The frozen per-holder file that shows the same names at roughly half the current aggregate: https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/data/short-positions-daily-update.xlsx (only sheet: 'Historic Disclosures 10.07.2026'; last Ceres row Marshall Wace 1.34% at 08/07/2026)

evidence.text: The royalty line -- the single number the December 2025 Grizzly Research short report says will never materialise -- will almost certainly still be immaterial in H1 2026: FY2025 royalties were GBP110k on total revenue of GBP32.6m, Ceres' own FY2025 framing is that royalties 'scale from 2027', and its only royalty-paying licensee, Doosan Fuel Cell, reported H1 2026 revenue of KRW189.1bn against KRW454.8bn a year earlier with a KRW52.2bn operating loss.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The first-ever royalty disclosure, in the FY2025 results of 26 Mar 2026, moved the stock +6.67% -- but that RNS was followed two minutes later by 'Ceres and Centrica sign a strategic partnership' at 07:02, so the royalty number itself has never been priced alone at this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Honestly, it mostly IS priced -- this is the shorts' core claim and 13.3% of the register is paid to hold it -- which is why it is [sizing note removed].5 rather than -3. It is also a weak proxy in the direction that cuts against me: Doosan's revenue fall is its legacy PAFC business, while its SOFC line went the other way (first overseas stack export, a KRW108.7bn Reverion order, a new 50MW factory). I keep it only because the royalty line is the marquee number in this print and a reader should see it sized rather than omitted.
evidence.independence: Ceres' own FY2025 statement that royalties scale from 2027 and that FY2025 royalties were GBP110k: https://www.ceres.tech/media/jpmpucda/ceres-power-holdings-plc-final-results-statement-2026-march-26.pdf ; the short thesis it restates: https://grizzlyreports.com/ceres/ (11 December 2025)

evidence.text: Delta Electronics is due to start pilot production of Ceres-based SOFC at Tainan 'by the end of 2026', which is the trigger for the next royalty step-up; nothing about it resolves on 23 September.

The RFC Power / Certain Energy spin-out completed on 26 August 2026 (Ceres retains c.37% plus a revenue share, contributed GBP1m cash and took GBP1.5m of equity for in-kind engineering) is a post-balance-sheet event: any deconsolidation gain lands in H2 2026, not in the half being reported.
Doosan's KRW108.7bn (c.GBP60m) SOFC stack supply contract with Reverion, announced 6 August 2026, converts to Ceres royalties only as stacks ship; no part of it is in the half being reported.

A company-published H1 2026 revenue or EBITDA expectation: none exists. Ceres has issued no trading update since the FY2025 results, and the 3 Sep 2026 Notice of Interim Results carries no numbers. The 9 June placing RNS carries a cash figure but, unusually for a UK placing, no trading commentary at all.

A quantified licence fee for Weichai: the 5 Nov 2025 RNS says only 'consistent with previous Ceres manufacturing licensing agreements' and names no figure, so the Delta GBP43m read-across is an inference and is sized as one.

Any commercial value attached to the Centrica partnership (26 Mar 2026) or the Delta/Centrica infrastructure partnership (30 Apr 2026): both RNSs disclose no licence fee, no revenue and no recognition timing.

A cause for the +15.48% five-day run-up in Ceres' own filings: there has been no RNS since 3 September 2026. The nearest explanation is sector flow -- FuelCell Energy +13%, Plug +7%, Bloom +3% on 17 Sep on a US House bill shifting data-centre power costs to operators, and Bloom's S&P 500 entry on 21 Sep -- which is a hypothesis about transmission, not a company fact, so I have not made a finding of it.
Investegate's UK short-positions page returns no per-company data to either curl or WebFetch; I used the FCA files directly instead.

Sharecast, Proactive Investors and the Investors' Chronicle are recorded in researcher_europe/LESSONS.md as 403 to both tools; I routed around them rather than spending calls, and their Ceres URLs surfaced in search results only.

The Ceres FY2025 and H1 2025 results PDFs on ceres.tech are font-subset PDFs that eu_pdftext.py reads only partially (H1 2025 returned no usable text); the H1 2025 line items quoted here come from the Investegate/press record, not from the PDF, and are marked as such.

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. evidence.text: The entire first half was pre-released eleven weeks ago, so the interims carry almost no surprise capacity on the reported numbers -- and [THE COMPANY]'s last two September interims, both preceded by a July trading update that pre-announced the half in exactly the same way, fell 3.08% (2024-09-24) and 1.75% (2025-09-30).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the line's own history: 2 of 2 prior interims down, -3.08% and -1.75%, mean -2.4%. Every large move this name has made came on a Trading Update (+8.65% 2025-07-24, -32.19% 2026-07-08) or on Full Year Results (+4.43%, +7.60%), never on interims. The 217-day UK median gap between scheduled releases is why: the trading update, not the interim, is where [THE COMPANY]'s price-sensitive information lands.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is largely priced and I have sized it accordingly -- this is the one finding here that AGREES with the sealed lean of -0.166 and with the +6.55% run-up, which is why it is cut to -0.6 rather than carrying the -2.4% mean of the two prior interims. What is not fully priced is the SCALE: the baseline's event_move_proxy of 3.16% is the median of all nine observed events and is dragged up by two trading updates at +8.65% and -32.19%. Conditioned on event type, this name's interims travel ~2.0-2.4%. Anyone sizing this print off the blended proxy is sizing it roughly 40% too wide.
evidence.independence: Corroborated by the Notice of Interim Results (2026-09-04), which schedules the event but pre-releases nothing further: [url removed] . Edison's note on the trading update says explicitly that it rebased 'pending better visibility when the company reports H126 results in September' -- i.e. the sell-side treats September as the visibility event, not a numbers event: [url removed] (2026-07-08).

evidence.text: FY26 guidance was set on 8 July, eight days after the half closed and with H1 actuals in hand, and its EBITDA leg is soft: guide $38-42m less H1's $19.3m implies H2 adj EBITDA of $18.7-22.7m against a derived H2-25 of about $19.9m -- roughly -6% to +14%, midpoint ~+4%, on a business that grew adj EBITDA 36% in FY25. A second cut eleven weeks after a guide set on actuals is a much lower-probability event than the July cut was.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line that moves this stock and it moves it violently: the FY26 cut on 2026-07-08 took it -32.19% in one session, the largest move in the nine-event history by a factor of four. The two upside guidance-bearing prints, FY24 results (2025-03-18) and FY25 results (2026-03-17), gave +4.43% and +7.60%. So this line pays asymmetrically when it surprises, and a mere reiteration -- which is my base case -- is worth far less than either tail.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced, and cut hard for it. [THE COMPANY] carries 8 analysts on $1.06m/day of turnover, which is the TOP of this stage's measured coverage band rather than the under-read $1-5m/5-7-analyst regime the thesis targets, so the sell-side has certainly built this bridge. What the wire copy carries is '[THE COMPANY] cuts guidance, shares slump 33%'; what it does not carry is that the resulting H2 EBITDA ask is ~+4% at the midpoint with the low end below prior year. The residual edge is with the marginal AIM price-setter reading the headline, not with the eight analysts.
evidence.independence: Different document, same direction: the 2026-07-08 trading update itself, which sets the guide and states the offsetting cost action -- [url removed] . NOTE ON DOUBLE-COUNTING: this finding and finding 3 (director buying) both argue 'the bar is beatable' from two independent documents; they are deliberately sized as a pair totalling +1.2, not as two full-size findings. CAVEAT ON THE ARITHMETIC: the H2-25 EBITDA base of ~$19.9m is DERIVED, not disclosed. FY25 adj EBITDA of $41.3m is confirmed in the document above, but the company gives H1-25 on an 'underlying' basis ($18.4m) and the FY25 RNS separately notes 'approximately $3m from launch-phase pricing related to a single Digital Wallet connection in H1 2025'. Adding that back gives reported H1-25 EBITDA of ~$21.4m and H2-25 of ~$19.9m. There is roughly $3m of uncertainty in that base, which is why the revenue leg of the same bridge (+3.9% to +14.6% H2 growth, midpoint ~+9.3%) is NOT claimed as undemanding -- it asks H2 to repeat H1's growth rate while the merchant dual-sourcing and the ~$4m/yr suspended DCB connection annualise into the H2 base. Only the EBITDA leg is load-bearing here.

evidence.text: The CEO bought 106,000 shares at 95p on 8 July 2026 -- the day of the 32% crash and the same day he set the FY26 guide -- and the CFO bought 65,000 at 98.75p on 10 July; both are now roughly 25-28% in the money at 122p.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No directly comparable prior instance in the nine-event history -- these are the only post-warning PDMR purchases in the observed record, so this line has no reaction distribution of its own on this name. That is the main reason it is [sizing note removed].4 rather than higher.
evidence.why_not_priced: PDMR RNS are filed at 15:30 and 11:33 on days when the stock had just fallen 32%, and no wire service carried them -- the July coverage is uniformly '[THE COMPANY] slumps 33%'. If this were priced, the stock would not have bottomed at 94.6p the same afternoon and taken ten weeks to recover to 122p. The amounts are small in absolute terms (~GBP 101k and ~GBP 64k) and that is exactly why it is [sizing note removed].4: it is a signal about management's own read of the guide they had just set, not a material transfer of ownership.
evidence.independence: Corroborated by the CFO's separate filing two days later, a different PDMR on a different date: [url removed] (2026-07-10, Robert Whittick, 65,000 shares at 98.75p). Points the same way as finding 2 and is sized as part of that pair.

evidence.text: Richard Griffiths -- founder of The Evolution Group and ORA Capital, a long-standing UK small-cap investor -- went from below 3% to 3.07% on 17 August and then to 4.25% on 18 September, converting his entire 1.05% CFD position into physical stock and adding ~3.35m shares of net new exposure; the second notification hit the wire at 17:09 on Monday 21 September, two days before the print.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not previously observable on this name -- Griffiths crossed 3% for the first time on 2026-08-17, so there is no prior instance of him accumulating into a [THE COMPANY] print. What the tape shows on the one day his buying is datable is that on 2026-09-11 the stock rose 5.36% (112.0p -> 118.0p) on 2,685,524 shares, roughly 4.6x the recent median, and that single session is essentially the whole of the baseline's +6.55% 20-day run-up.
evidence.why_not_priced: A TR-1 filed at 17:09 on a Monday evening is the single least-read regulated disclosure in the UK market: no wire carries it, it has no headline, and this stage's own positioning anchor -- the FCA aggregated NET SHORT register -- is structurally blind to long accumulation by construction. If it were priced, the baseline's priced_lean_pct would not read the +6.55% run-up as a -0.328 negative, because that run-up is not diffuse anticipation of a good print: it is one identifiable buyer absorbing one identifiable seller. Moving from CFD to physical is the part that is hard to explain as trading -- it surrenders leverage and takes on settlement and voting, which is what a holder does when he intends to stay.
evidence.independence: Different filer, same register, and it is the other side of the same transfer: BlackRock's reducing TR-1 of 2026-09-14 puts its threshold crossing on 2026-09-11, the exact session of the +5.36% move on 4.6x volume -- [url removed] . Third, independent corroboration that the September re-rating was NOT the company's own bid: [THE COMPANY]'s buyback DECELERATED across the rally, 148,571 shares over 20-26 Aug at ~113.9p, 90,488 over 3-9 Sep at ~111.77p, then only 50,000 over 10-16 Sep at 120.00p -- [url removed] . NOTE: finding 5 is the opposite side of this same register and the two are netted, not summed independently.

evidence.text: BlackRock has filed three reducing TR-1s in two months -- 6.75%, then 6.37% on 11 August, then 5.87% on 11 September, about 1.48m shares between the last two notifications alone -- and still holds 5.87%, so a demonstrated, persistent seller is live into the highest-volume session of the half.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately observable in the nine-event history. The one datable instance is 2026-09-11, when BlackRock crossed below 6% and the stock nonetheless rose 5.36% on 2.69m shares -- i.e. on the only day we can price this seller's flow, the supply was absorbed with the price UP. That is why this is -0.5 rather than larger.
evidence.why_not_priced: Same structural reason as finding 4 -- TR-1s carry no headline and no wire, and the sealed positioning anchor reads only the short register. But the honest read is that this is the WEAKER half of the transfer and it is sized as such: BlackRock's reductions look like passive/quant rebalancing rather than informed selling, and Griffiths' ~3.35m shares of net buying exceeds the ~2.5m BlackRock has shed across both notifications. Filed as a separate finding because it resolves against a different counterparty, but netted against finding 4 rather than summed as an independent negative.
evidence.independence: Same register, opposite direction to finding 4 -- explicitly netted with it (+0.8 and -0.5 for a net +0.3 of positioning), not counted twice. The prior leg is a separate document: [url removed] (2026-08-12, 6.75% -> 6.37%, crossing 2026-08-11).
