The only Holding(s) in Company RNS since (16 Sept, 13:23) is a technical transfer of the existing River UK Micro Cap holding to Liontrust at 6.0659% on an FCA change-of-control approval, not a purchase. So the marginal buyer of the gap is undisclosed and sub-3% - retail and momentum, not a re-rating by a holder who will sit through a disappointing statement. If the market had priced a durable re-rating the stock would have held 195p rather than drifting to 183.5p on falling volume, and at least one 3% notification would exist.
evidence.independence: The cause is corroborated by a second, independent domestic outlet on a different date: Share Talk's weekly small-cap movers, 31 Aug 2026 - 'Kooth (AIM: KOO) rebounded 32.2% to 195p after Canaccord Genuity highlighted potential opportunities arising from the $18 billion Meta settlement' - https://www.share-talk.com/share-talk-weekly-small-cap-movers-shakers-monday-31st-august-2026/. The settlement's terms are independently sourced to the California Attorney General's own release, https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-bonta-secures-transformative-17-billion-settlement-meta (2026-08-26).

evidence.text: The FY2026 revenue bar requires an H2 that reverses the trend of the last five halves. Kooth's own compiled consensus (10 Apr 2026) is FY26 revenue GBP63.1m; H1 2026 came in at GBP30.8m, so H2 must deliver GBP32.3m against an H2 2025 of GBP31.2m (FY25 GBP63.3m less H1 25 GBP32.088m) - +3.5% year on year - while California product development revenue continues 'planned tapering' and sterling is running ~1% stronger against the dollar in H2 2026 (~1.342) than in H2 2025 (~1.33). H1 2026 revenue itself FELL 4.0% year on year. The 29 July trading update reaffirmed only the HALF ('Performance for the half year ended 30 June 2026 is in line with expectations') and made no FY26 statement at all; 23 September is the first FY26 outlook statement since 8 April.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is precisely the line that sold the 2025 print. At the 23 Sept 2025 H1 results - also preceded by a July trading update - Kooth's outlook section quantified an FX haircut for the first time ('the expected impact would be to reduce full year consensus median revenue of GBP66.8m by c.2-3% and consensus median adjusted EBITDA of GBP10.2m by c.6-8%') and the stock fell 5.00% on the day, the baseline's second-largest negative reaction. The 29 July 2026 half-year trading update, which likewise declined to address the full year, fell 3.50%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Net of the rest of the company, this is a genuine two-sided call and that is why I size it small: H2 2026 gets the first full half of the State of Michigan contract ($2.6m annualised, signed only in January 2026 after the delays Kooth blamed for FY25), the DWP-funded employment-and-mental-health programmes launching across the West Midlands, South Yorkshire and Cambridgeshire, 14 new UK contracts, and the UK Soluna launch into the autumn school term. Those could carry GBP32.3m. What is unpriced is that with FOUR analysts covering a name doing $228k/day, nobody has published a refreshed FY26 model since April - the consensus page the market is anchored to is 5.5 months old and predates both the July update and the Meta-note re-rating. If the market had worked the arithmetic the stock would not be 63% below its own consensus 303-330p target with zero published preview.
evidence.independence: The H1 2025 comparative that fixes H2 2025 at GBP31.2m is from a different document - the audited-basis H1 2025 results PDF, https://investors.kooth.com/docs/koothplclibraries/archive/results/half-year-results-2025.pdf (total revenue 32,088). Shares the 29 July 2026 trading update RNS with nothing else in this list, since I dropped the reported-quarter finding that also rested on it.

evidence.text: Adjusted EBITDA is where Kooth has systematically sandbagged, and the FY26 bar looks low. At the 23 Sept 2025 H1 results Kooth guided FY25 consensus adjusted EBITDA of GBP10.2m down by 'c.6-8%' for FX - an implied GBP9.4-9.6m - and then delivered GBP11.3m, described in its own FY25 RNS as 'ahead of expectations': an ~18% beat against its own guided number. FY26 consensus adjusted EBITDA is GBP10.4m; H1 2026 alone is GBP5.0-5.4m against H1 2025's GBP1.6m, so H2 has only to match H1 to clear it, and the H1 2025 margin drag (gross margin -19.6ppt on front-loaded California user marketing, 'intentionally weighted towards H1 2025') is not repeating. Net cash also ROSE in the half, GBP21.6m at Dec 2025 to GBP23.1m at Jun 2026, so the -GBP6.58m cash generation that accompanied the 2025 print is absent.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: When Kooth has confirmed or beaten on adjusted EBITDA the market has paid: +11.74% on the 28 Jan 2026 Trading Update and +4.67% on the 8 Apr 2026 Full Year Results, the two most recent scheduled releases in the baseline where the EBITDA line was the good news. The offsetting precedent is that an EBITDA beat has never been enough on its own when the outlook section carried a haircut (23 Sept 2025, -5.00%), which is why this is sized below the two negatives combined rather than above them.
evidence.why_not_priced: The valuation says nobody has done this sum. At 183.5p on 36,694,683 shares the market capitalisation is ~GBP67m and, less GBP23.1m of net cash, the enterprise value is ~GBP44m - 4.2x the FY26 consensus adjusted EBITDA of GBP10.4m, for a business whose H1 adjusted EBITDA tripled. If the market had priced an EBITDA beat the stock would be trading on the run-up it got from a Meta read-through rather than despite a 4.2x EV/EBITDA, and at least one of the four brokers would have published a raised number since 10 April; none has. The honest counterweight, and the reason this is +1.3 and not +3: FY26 consensus diluted EPS of 6.8p puts the same stock on 27x earnings, so the gap between adjusted EBITDA and statutory profit is large (capitalised development amortisation), and the results statement is exactly where that gap becomes visible line by line.
evidence.independence: The FY25 outcome is from a separate RNS on a separate date: '2025 revenue was GBP63.3m (2024: GBP66.7m)... Adjusted EBITDA was ahead of expectations at GBP11.3m in 2025 (2024: GBP15.8m)' - https://investors.kooth.com/rns-alerts/archive/2026/080426.asp (2026-04-08). The FY26 consensus level is from the company's analyst-consensus page, which this finding shares with the revenue finding above; the two use the same page for OPPOSITE lines (revenue vs EBITDA) and are otherwise independent.

evidence.text: The California cliff is the dominant value driver and it resolves far outside this window. California's CYBHI Behavioral Health Virtual Services Platform funding - Soluna plus Brightline's BrightLife Kids, a $680m state commitment of which Kooth's share has been reported at $271m over four years - runs to 30 June 2027, and Kooth has 'now entered the fourth year of the contract'. FY2027 consensus revenue of GBP60.8m (only -3.6% on FY26) implicitly assumes continuity or replacement. Any re-procurement decision, and any actual allocation of California's $1.5-2.1bn Meta settlement share to a youth mental-health platform, lands in 2027 and later - not on 23 September. Management may reference it; it cannot be resolved in one session.

The Meta settlement itself was still awaiting judicial approval when it was announced on 26 August 2026, and California's payment is structured over ten years. Court approval and any state-level appropriation of those funds are the events that would validate the 27-28 August re-rating, and both sit well past 23 September 2026.

options.reason: No European single-stock option chain is retrievable from a free source. Yahoo returns 0 expiries and 0 contracts for .L, .DE and .PA symbols against 21 and 196 for AAPL on the same crumb; Eurex's daily reference file carries trading parameters but no settlement prices, no open interest and no underlying ISIN map, and its statistics page is JavaScript with no JSON endpoint. So there is no event-implied move and no skew, and this baseline supplies its own priced_lean_pct and anchor_quality from the national short registers instead. This holds for all ten markets; nothing measured in 2026-09 on …

consensus.basis: Sell-side coverage, carried because it is the measurable proxy for this stage's thesis. Phase 1 measured 1-2 analysts below $1m/day of turnover, 5-7 at $1-5m, 11-13 at $5-25m and 16-19 above, consistently across all three markets. eu_resolve.py ranks the hunt BY this band so the thesis is tested rather than selected on.

history.caveat: Dates are REAL: each row is a results announcement the market's own archive records on that date, and the move is over this stage's own window. Only the UK (Investegate) and Norway (Oslo NewsWeb) reach this state; the other eight markets are estimated.

event_plausibility.basis: vendor forward calendar (TradingView), measured at a 2.2% phantom rate on 90 UK rows against the RNS record. Confirmation against Investegate (RNS mirror) is eu_resolve.py's job, after the fact.

positioning.basis: sum of disclosed net short positions at or above 0.5% of shares outstanding, as published by the national regulator

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Phase 1 median realised move was 2.81% (UK), 3.12% (DE), 4.19% (FR) against Japan's 2.87%, with the tail intact in all three -- 42%, 27% and 52% maxima and no price limit to truncate them.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read eu_priced_in.lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR borrowed from the US runs, none is measured on European data, and eu_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

anchor_coverage.basis: `anchor_covered` is true only where the national short register returned a disclosed net short position for THIS issuer. A name the register was read for and does not name reads 0.0 -- real, but the 0.5% truncation floor rather than a measurement, and below $1m/day of turnover 168 of 190 sampled UK issuers read exactly that. The turnover floor moved from $1m to $200k on 2026-09-19, so this field is how the cost of that move is made visible: eu_resolve.py reports the Spearman split by it, with the count in each arm.

anchor_quality.basis: magnitude: realised vol plus a reaction history, capped at 0.5 because neither is an option-implied move. direction: how many of the two positioning components resolved, capped at 0.45 because neither is 25-delta skew and Europe has no margin-balance component to add, and held to 0.15 where the register was read and does not name this issuer -- a truncated zero is not a disclosure.

evidence.text: The company's own 23 July RNS pre-announces H1 adjusted EPS of 38p-42p and, in a footnote, puts FY2026 consensus at 202.8p -- so the 'in line' the market is holding requires roughly 162p of H2 adjusted EPS, about four times H1 and an ~80/20 split, against 141.4p/133.9p (51/49) in 2025; the same RNS reports the order book at 17.3 weeks, which reads as improvement only against the FY25 year-end 15.7 but is flat against the like-for-like H1 2025 comparator of 17.4 weeks printed in the same sentence, and on a sales base 21% lower is roughly 21% smaller in absolute terms, with order intake down 11%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Judges has downgraded or disappointed at three of its last five scheduled statements and the stock moved -11.61% (Trading Update 2024-11-18), -15.19% (Half Year Trading Update 2025-07-24) and about -11% (Full Year Trading Statement 2026-01-22, Proactive) on those days -- so when this line surprises on this name it surprises double-digit and the UK tail is not truncated. But the two September interims in the observed RNS history moved only -4.27% (2024-09-19) and +1.91% (2025-09-18), because the July trading update had already carried the half-year news both times; and the 2026-07-23 update itself, which contained the 38-42p, the -21% revenue and the Geotek slip to 2028, moved the stock only -1.62% (4625.0 -> 4550.0, Yahoo daily closes) and it closed higher the next day.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 202.8p footnote and the 38-42p are both public, but no source I could reach does the division. Every piece of secondary coverage I found reported the flattering order-book comparator (Sharecast/Halifax and the Stockopedia brief both frame it as '17.3 weeks compared with 15.7 weeks at the end of 2025') and none states the implied H2 EPS or the 80/20 split. This is a 4-analyst, GBP 250m AIM name trading about USD 446k a day, so the marginal price-setter is a retail or adviser reader of exactly that wire summary. If the arithmetic were priced you would not see all four published targets sitting above spot (average 6450p, Berenberg buy 5600p reiterated 25 July 2026, and even Jefferies' underperform target of 4015p is 7% above the 3750p spot) and you would not see the whole 19% de-rating since 23 July happen on a median 8,030 shares a day with no analyst revision in between.
evidence.independence: Separately corroborated as a fact pattern by the company's 22 January 2026 statement, which guided FY2026 to 200-250p explicitly 'assuming no rebound in US demand and no contribution from Geotek's next coring expedition' -- and the July RNS then pushed that expedition from early 2027 to 'no earlier than 2028', so the FY26 bar has not moved while the 2027 support under it has been removed: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/judges-scientific-says-starts-2026-with-lower-than-desired-order-book-ce7e58d2de8ff725 (2026-01-22). Note this finding deliberately merges what were two sizes in my pre-local draft (the H2 arithmetic and the order-book framing) because both rest on the same RNS document.

evidence.text: The Investegate regulated-news record shows Judges has filed nothing price-sensitive in the 61 days since it reaffirmed FY2026 -- only a Notice of Investor Presentation (12 Aug) and two Share Incentive Plan PDMR notices (6 Aug, 10 Sep) -- from an issuer that publishes its own consensus number and has a demonstrated habit of putting bad news out in a standalone RNS, which under MAR Article 17 makes two months of silence evidence the board does not presently believe 202.8p is materially unachievable.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three times this board concluded it would miss, it said so in a dedicated RNS and the stock fell double digits the same morning (2024-11-18 -11.61%, 2025-07-24 -15.19%, 2026-01-22 about -11%). The two times it reached September interims without having warned first, the reaction was -4.27% (2024) and +1.91% (2025). So the informative event for this name has historically been the warning RNS, not the results RNS.
evidence.why_not_priced: An absence is not a headline and no aggregator emits it; you can only establish it from a complete domestic RNS mirror, which is what Investegate is. The price is behaving as if a warning were coming -- the stock is at 3750p, 2.7% off its 52-week low of 3650p and 41% below the 6360p high, having fallen 19% from 4625p on 22 July -- but it got there on a median 8,030 shares a day (about GBP 300k), which is a thin tape with no bid rather than a market verdict. If the market had weighed the silence you would expect the drift to have stopped or reversed as the 30-day closed period began around 24 August; instead the stock made new lows on 16, 17, 21 and 22 September. Deliberately sized small and its band crosses zero, because this board has never issued a truly out-of-cycle warning -- it uses its scheduled January and July statements -- and 23 September is itself a scheduled slot it could use.
evidence.independence: The six PDMR notices since July are all automatic Share Incentive Plan or dividend-reinvestment purchases of 6 to 8 shares each at 4450.0p (05/08/2026) and 4175.0p (07/09/2026), so nothing in the insider record contradicts or corroborates the silence in either direction -- there is no discretionary director buying at the low either: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/judges-scientific--jdg/director-pdmr-shareholding/9766456 (2026-09-10).

evidence.text: The bullish half of the baseline's positioning lean is stale and belongs to one manager's profit-taking: the FCA per-holder record shows GLG Partners LP peaked at 1.82% on 2026-02-11 and filed a monotonic 1.78 / 1.68 / 1.58 / 1.47 / 1.36 through 19 May 2026 while the stock fell 41%, and the aggregate has sat at 1.67% since position date 17/08/2026 with no filing in the five weeks since, during which the stock fell another 3.8%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior on this name for a short-covering reaction. What the record does show is that the covering flow has not supported the price at any point: GLG [sizing note removed].82% to 1.36% between February and May 2026 and the stock fell from roughly 6000p to 4500p over the same stretch, and it cut again into mid-August while the stock fell from 4550p to 3900p.
evidence.why_not_priced: The sealed baseline read only the aggregated register, which shows one number and one change (1.67%, -0.52pp) and scores it as `short_building` +1.040 -- a bullish component worth nearly half the +2.295 lean. The per-holder history, which only the FCA's own per-holder file and Investegate's mirror of it carry, shows that change is the tail of a seven-month orderly reduction by a single manager into a 41% decline, and that it stopped five weeks before the print. I am NOT claiming the other half of the lean back: 111,234 shares against 8,030 a day is 13.9 sessions to cover and that squeeze constraint is real, but it is already what `short_squeeze` +1.002 is paying for and I will not double-count it. So this finding is only the correction to the stale component.

evidence.text: Judges has a written dividend policy of 'increasing dividends by no less than 10% per annum', which implies a 36.0p interim on 23 September against pre-announced H1 adjusted EPS of 38p-42p -- cover of about 1.1x, against 4.3x on the 32.7p paid a year ago.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line has never surprised: the company raised the interim 10% to 32.7p in 2025 and the final 10% to 82.3p at the 31 March 2026 prelims -- a day the stock rose 4.48% on results that the same release called disappointing, with the dividend increase the headline positive most coverage led with.
evidence.why_not_priced: The four analysts will model +10% and the increase itself is not news; what is not modelled anywhere I could reach is that policy compliance now costs the board almost all of first-half earnings, so the declaration is a costly signal rather than a formality and the market is not positioned to read it as one with the stock at a 52-week low. Sized small and with a band that reaches -2.0 because the downside case -- the first break of a policy this company has honoured every year since 2008 -- would be read as a pre-emptive admission about the second half. If the market were pricing that risk the stock would not be holding a roughly 18.5x multiple on the 202.8p consensus.
evidence.independence: The facility terms in the same document make a forced cut unlikely and therefore cap this finding's downside: 'GBP 90m RCF alongside a GBP 50m uncommitted accordion facility ... history.caveat: Dates are ESTIMATED by stepping the measured cadence gap backwards from the vendor's last release date; the move is the largest within +/-2 trading days of that estimate. A cadence prior, not a record that a print happened on that date. Use it as a SCALE for how far this name travels, never as evidence about a particular past date -- TRT was ranked, traded and never reported on exactly this mistake.

event_plausibility.basis: vendor forward calendar (TradingView), measured at a 2.2% phantom rate on 90 UK rows against the RNS record. Confirmation against EQS-News search (per issuer, paginated, back years) is eu_resolve.py's job, after the fact.

positioning.basis: absent from a register that downloaded successfully, so no disclosed net short position at or above the 0.5% public threshold. A real zero -- but the threshold truncates, so 0.4% and 0.0% are both recorded here as 0.0, and the join is on the issuer NAME, so a name spelled differently in the register reads as a zero it should not.

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Phase 1 median realised move was 2.81% (UK), 3.12% (DE), 4.19% (FR) against Japan's 2.87%, with the tail intact in all three -- 42%, 27% and 52% maxima and no price limit to truncate them.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read eu_priced_in.lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR borrowed from the US runs, none is measured on European data, and eu_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

anchor_coverage.basis: `anchor_covered` is true only where the national short register returned a disclosed net short position for THIS issuer. A name the register was read for and does not name reads 0.0 -- real, but the 0.5% truncation floor rather than a measurement, and below $1m/day of turnover 168 of 190 sampled UK issuers read exactly that. The turnover floor moved from $1m to $200k on 2026-09-19, so this field is how the cost of that move is made visible: eu_resolve.py reports the Spearman split by it, with the count in each arm.

anchor_quality.basis: magnitude: realised vol plus a reaction history, capped at 0.5 because neither is an option-implied move. direction: how many of the two positioning components resolved, capped at 0.45 because neither is 25-delta skew and Europe has no margin-balance component to add, and held to 0.15 where the register was read and does not name this issuer -- a truncated zero is not a disclosure.

evidence.text: [THE COMPANY]'s results days are systematically sold - the last six actual print days all closed lower (2024-09-26 -0.91%, 2025-02-13 -9.49%, 2025-05-13 -6.30%, 2025-09-25 -3.13%, 2026-02-12 -7.42%, 2026-05-12 -2.31%; five of six also underperformed the SDAX) - and this year's number is NOT pre-released: [THE COMPANY]'s own ad-hoc register carries no filing since 2025-09-24, so there is no Prognoseanpassung and no preliminary-figures ad-hoc standing between the market and the full-year number. The stock goes in at EUR 77.80, +15.4% over 60 sessions and 2.6% below a 52-week high set on 2026-09-09.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This IS the reaction history. Six of six prints negative over two years, mean -4.93%, median absolute move 4.72%. The one print that was substantially pre-released by an ad-hoc (16 August 2024 preliminary figures) produced the smallest fall, -0.91% - but even that day underperformed a +2.74% SDAX by 3.65 points. The two prints where the operating number IMPROVED (9M FY24/25 and 9M FY25/26, EBITDA +7.2%) still fell 6.30% and 2.31%. Beats on this name have been sold.
evidence.why_not_priced: The baseline itself is the demonstration. Its history block is basis 'estimated_from_cadence' and its eight inferred dates (2025-08-14, 2026-01-02, 2026-05-12...) mostly land on non-event days, which is why it reports a median absolute move of 2.09% and an event_move_proxy of 2.09%. The real print days are 2025-09-25, 2026-02-12 and 2026-05-12 and their absolute moves are 3.13%, 7.42% and 2.31%. If the market were positioned for this, the 2026-02-12 guidance cut would not have taken 7.42% out of the stock in one session on a name with five analysts, and the price would not be sitting within 2.6% of its 52-week high two days before an un-pre-released annual print. No broker has published on the name since 20.07.2026 (Baader, Add, target 78->85).
evidence.independence: The vendor-independent confirmation that nothing has been pre-released is [THE COMPANY]'s own newsroom, whose only item since 2026-05-12 is the 2026-09-09 conference-call notice: [url removed] . The reaction-day closes are computed from [url removed] and the index comparison from [url removed] - a different series from the ad-hoc register, so the two legs of this finding do not rest on one document, but the run-up and the reaction distribution DO share the [url removed] tape and are therefore filed as one finding rather than two.

evidence.text: The FY2026/2027 outlook given on 23 September has to lap three things that do not repeat: a ~EUR 30m one-off from the sale of licensing rights tied to the North American corn divestiture, a EUR 7.7m participation gain from selling the AgReliant JV stakes, and the AgReliant equity income itself - on top of a Russian business [THE COMPANY] says is still shrinking. That is against a medium-term frame of 3-5% organic growth and a 19-21% EBITDA margin set on 2025-09-25, which [THE COMPANY] already missed once when it cut FY25/26 growth from ~3% to flat on 2026-02-12. Reported group EBITDA is therefore likely to be guided DOWN year on year even if the margin band is held.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line is where this stock's biggest moves have come from. 2026-02-12, comparable sales guidance cut from ~3% to flat with the margin band held: -7.42%. 2025-02-13, the equivalent H1 guidance event a year earlier: -9.49%. 2025-09-25, FY24/25 results setting the 3% FY25/26 guide plus the new three-year 3-5% / 19-21% medium-term frame: -3.13%. All three negative, and the two that changed a number were the two largest.
evidence.why_not_priced: The English-language record carries the EUR 29m one-off as a line in the 9M release but not the second item - the EUR 7.7m participation gain - and nowhere joins them to the FY26/27 base. The AgReliant divestiture ad-hoc of 2025-06-27 quantified the proceeds only as 'a low three-digit million range (USD)'; there is no public number for the equity income [THE COMPANY] loses with it. With five analysts and no published note since 20.07.2026, nobody has walked the market through an FY26/27 EBITDA base that is roughly EUR 30m lower before a single operating assumption is made. If this were priced, the stock would not be trading 2.6% off its high into the release, and the July target raise (78->85) would have been accompanied by a cut to FY26/27 estimates.
evidence.independence: The EUR 29m one-off is independently stated by the issuer in English in the 9M release, [url removed] ('a positive one-time operating effect of EUR 29 million arose from the sale of licensing rights in connection with the divestiture of the North American corn business'), and the disposal itself by the ad-hoc of 2025-06-27, [url removed] . The medium-term 3-5% / 19-21% frame is from the FY24/25 release, [url removed] .

evidence.text: The 2027 German sugarbeet contracting round is already settled and it came out BETTER than the two preceding years, which [THE COMPANY] can underwrite in its FY26/27 outlook: the SZVG - the growers' cooperative that holds the majority stake in Suedzucker - has released 100% of delivery rights for the 2027 cultivation contract, cancelling the 90% restriction imposed in spring, explicitly because of the expected fall in sugar output from the 2026 harvest. Sugarbeet is EUR 324.6m of [THE COMPANY]'s EUR 386.8m 9M group EBITDA, and European beet seed is billed in the Jan-Mar quarter that sits inside FY26/27.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent: [THE COMPANY] has guided European beet acreage DOWN at each of its last three releases and the stock fell each time (-3.13%, -7.42%, -2.31%). There is no observation in the last two years of [THE COMPANY] guiding beet area up, so this is the first time the segment narrative could turn and the reaction is unmodelled - which is the argument for a real but bounded positive rather than a large one.
evidence.why_not_priced: The English-language coverage of EU sugar in August and September 2026 is entirely about the PRICE and the CROP - NW European sugar at EUR 550/t on 3 September, +40% year to date, EU 2026/27 output cut to a 38-year low - and says nothing about the contracting decisions that actually set how much beet seed [THE COMPANY] sells. Those decisions live on a German growers' cooperative website and in the German farm press, in German, and they are the transmission mechanism. If the market had read them, the sell-side would have a published FY26/27 European beet-volume assumption, and there is no note on the name since 20.07.2026. Sized small deliberately, for three reasons the same German sources give: the SZVG decision covers southern Germany only, a fraction of [THE COMPANY]'s global beet seed book; Nordzucker's agreed 2027 minimum price is EUR 31.00/t, below prior years; and Pfeifer & Langen has cut more than 80 growers with ~1,200 ha out of 2027 contracts altogether. This is a direct counterparty in the beet chain speaking, not [THE COMPANY], so it is a hypothesis about [THE COMPANY]'s guidance until [THE COMPANY] says it.
evidence.independence: The opposite-signed German evidence, which is why this is +0.8 and not larger: top agrar 2026-04-23, [url removed] - 'liegt der vereinbarte Ruebenmindestpreis bei 31,00 EUR/t Ruebe bei einem Zuckergehalt von 18,0 % - und damit aufgrund der herausfordernden Lage am Zuckermarkt unter dem der Vorjahre', with the subscription window 7 May to 4 June 2026; and agrarheute 2026-05-21, [url removed] - 'Mehr als 80 Betriebe mit zusammen rund 1.200 Hektar Ruebenflaeche erhalten kein neues Vertragsangebot mehr.' The same-signed independent evidence is the EU sugar balance: [url removed] .

evidence.text: The reported quarter should land at or above the top of the guided band. 9M FY25/26 EBITDA of EUR 386.8m already exceeds the ENTIRE FY24/25 EBITDA of EUR 350.5m; prior-year 9M EBITDA was EUR 360.8m, so FY24/25's fourth quarter ran at -EUR 10.3m of EBITDA. Repeating that seasonal Q4 puts FY25/26 EBITDA near EUR 375m on roughly EUR 1.68bn of sales - about 22% reported, and about 20.7% stripping the ~EUR 29-30m licensing one-off, i.e. the upper half of the guided 19-21%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sold both times it has happened recently. 2026-05-12: 9M EBITDA +7.2%, sales +2.6% comparable, guidance held - stock -2.31%. 2025-05-13: 9M results that the company called robust - stock -6.30%. This is precisely why the finding is [sizing note removed].6 and the emitted move is negative: on this name a good operating number has not bought a positive session.
evidence.why_not_priced: It largely IS priced - this is arithmetic any reader of the 9M release can do, which is why it carries +0.6 and not more. It is in the set because a hunt that only lists negatives on a name whose operating trend is improving is not answering the question honestly, and because it is the reason print_vs_bar_pct is positive while expected_move_pct is not. The only genuinely unmodelled part is that the ex-one-off margin lands in the upper half rather than the middle of the band.
evidence.independence: The prior-year 9M EBITDA of EUR 360.8m, which makes the Q4 derivation possible, is from a different release: [url removed] . The FY24/25 full-year EBITDA of EUR 350.5m and the 20.9% margin are from [url removed] (2025-09-25, 07:00 CEST). Flagged as DERIVED: the EUR 375m FY figure is my arithmetic from three sourced company numbers, not a figure any document states.

evidence.text: The FY25 annual report discloses that Group sales for the four months to 30 April 2026 were approximately GBP26.1m against GBP32.6m in the same four months of 2025 -- down 20% and already including Barry M from 9 February -- while the same document identifies GBP5.7m of non-repeating losses in the 2025 comparative (GBP2.4m of US tariff-driven Christmas order disruption plus GBP3.3m from a large Technic customer entering administration). Net of the easy comparative, the house broker's FY26 revenue of GBP108.0m still requires an H2 of roughly GBP63.5m against a normalised H2-25 of about GBP61.5m, on a base that ran -20% for a third of the year; the FY25 report also shows the core business excluding Brand Architekts at GBP93.3m against GBP102m in 2024. I size the pair net at -3.0 rather than treating the -20% alone as a large negative, because the comparative genuinely is soft.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the line that has moved the stock every time. 2025-09-10 interims cut FY guidance to GBP107-112m revenue and the shares fell 18.25%; 2025-02-06 trading update -19.17%; 2026-04-29 FY25 results, which carried this very four-month figure, -8.27%. The one positive print in the observed five (2026-02-09, +10.50%) was an acquisition headline, not a guidance line.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is public but it is not what the market is anchored on, and the anchoring was done by the company. The 2026-06-16 AGM Statement gave only a two-month window -- 'sales from 1 April to 31 May 2026 ahead of the same period last year' -- and no year-to-date figure at all, six weeks after the company had volunteered a four-month YTD number. Every piece of wire copy since June reports 'Q2 improves, full-year expectations unchanged'. If the arithmetic were priced, the stock would not have rallied 23.6% off 177p on 20 July to 218.6p, and the house broker's FY26 revenue would not still sit above FY25 actuals; with 3 analysts of whom 2 are paid by the company, nobody independent is publishing the H2 bridge.

evidence.text: The board halved its own forward EPS hurdle. Options granted on 17 June 2026 at 220p vest only if 'the compound annual growth rate in the Company's Adjusted Basic earnings per share must exceed 5 per cent. over the three financial years commencing 1 January 2026'; the previous grant, 5 December 2024, required the same metric to 'exceed 10 per cent. over the three financial years commencing 1 January 2025'. Off the FY25 adjusted EPS base of 16.7p, a 5% CAGR is 19.3p by FY2028 -- below the house broker's FY2026 forecast of 20.0p. The remuneration committee is calibrating three years of incentives to an outcome the published FY26 number already exceeds, and it did so the day after the AGM statement reiterated full-year expectations.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance of an option-hurdle reset on this name to score. The line it predicts -- the FY26/FY27 outlook paragraph -- is the one that produced -18.25% (2025-09-10) and -8.27% (2026-04-29). Scored on that line, not on the grant itself.
evidence.why_not_priced: A 'Grant of Options and Director/PDMR Shareholding' RNS is the single least-read headline category on AIM, and the comparison that makes it informative requires note 23 of a 108-page annual report, where the 10% hurdle sits. No wire story, no aggregator and no trade-press item I found mentions either hurdle. If it were priced, the 338p sell-side target on a 218p stock would not be standing and the June 2026 grant would not have been struck at 220p with a lower bar than the December 2024 grant struck at 490p. I size it -3.0 rather than larger because a 5% CAGR is a common minimum vesting gate and because the Dec-2024 grant is 55% underwater, so part of this reset is mechanical repricing after a de-rating rather than a forecast.
evidence.independence: The FY25 annual report, note 23, is the source of the superseded 10% hurdle and is a different document from the RNS: [url removed] . Fully independent of finding 1's evidence base (grant terms vs sales figures), though both documents are company-issued.

evidence.text: The baseline's free control is misreading what is priced. run_up_20d_pct is +0.24% and run_up_5d_pct -0.67%, but the stock bottomed at 177p on 20 July and closed at 218.55p on 22 September -- +23.6% -- and roughly a fifth of the volume that did it was the issuer's own bid. Treasury shares went from nil to 1,116,967 between 27 July and 16 September; the 1,020,364 bought after 3 August are 19.4% of the 5.27m shares that traded in those sessions, on a name whose median turnover is USD 384k a day. The RNS itself warned purchases 'could exceed 25 per cent of the average daily trading volume'. So the stock goes into this print at the top of a corporately-supported rally, not flat.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The one observed print preceded by a rally rather than a fall -- 2025-09-10 interims, after the stock had recovered through the summer -- produced the largest negative in the set at -18.25%. The two prints that followed weakness (2025-04-29, -3.70%) were milder. Small n, and stated as such.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is not a fact about the company, it is a fact about the measurement: the 20-day window starts on 24 August, three weeks after the rally had already happened, so every ranker that reads run_up_20d_pct sees a neutral name. Reconstructing it needs the weekly Transaction in Own Shares RNSs, the treasury share count in each, and the daily tape -- three sources no aggregator joins. If the market had priced the corporate bid out, September volume would not have collapsed to 58k-150k shares a day against 300-800k in July.
evidence.independence: The daily tape is a different source and shows the same thing: [url removed] (177p on 2026-07-20, 218.55p on 2026-09-22). This finding shares the buyback programme with the outside_window row below; the in-window content here is the price level going in, the out-of-window content there is the bid disappearing.

evidence.text: Barry M was bought on 9 February 2026 for GBP1.4m cash, including 'its IP, stock and order book, but excluding the manufacturing capabilities and any liabilities' -- a brand with GBP15-17.4m of annual turnover and one-metre-plus stands in 1,300 UK stores. No fair value allocation has ever been published: the FY25 annual report carries it only as a bare post-balance-sheet note. If the identifiable net assets acquired (inventory plus the order book plus brand IP) fair-value above GBP1.4m, IFRS 3 forces a gain on bargain purchase straight through the H1 income statement, which would flatter statutory PBT against a weak underlying half.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Barry M headline itself is the only positive print in the observed five: 2026-02-09 'Acquisition of Barry M brand & FY25 Trading Update' +10.50%, on a day that also carried a weak trading statement. So this market has paid for Barry M news before. No prior exceptional-credit instance to score.
evidence.why_not_priced: Because the number does not exist anywhere yet -- the H1 accounts are the first time IFRS 3 fair values for Barry M will be published, and the FY25 annual report deliberately says nothing beyond the consideration. It is [sizing note removed]; the company reports on adjusted EBITDA, which would exclude it, so the upside is confined to a statutory headline read by the RNS-reading retail half of the register.
evidence.independence: Barry M's scale is corroborated outside the company: GBP17.4m turnover for the year to February 2024 and 1,300 stores (Superdrug 650, Boots 420, Sainsbury's 120, Tesco 50) per [url removed] . The exclusion of the London factory is the offsetting risk and is on the record in the same trade piece.

evidence.text: The TR-1 record shows the largest non-insider holder adding into the print and a smaller one trimming: Schroders plc went 10.040844% -> 11.086664% on 16 June 2026, the day of the AGM statement; Rathbones Investment Management went 5.575700% -> 4.996700% on 6 July 2026. Against a concert party (Bazini, Macleod, Rodol and relatives) of about 39.73%, that leaves a genuinely thin free float -- roughly 44% once Schroders and Rathbones are removed -- which is the mechanical reason this name prints double-digit reactions on USD 384k of daily turnover.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior instance. Recorded here because it is the only disclosed positioning that exists for this name -- the FCA short register does not name it -- and because it is the main reason I did not size the negative findings closer to the 10.5% median.
evidence.why_not_priced: TR-1 notifications on a GBP175m AIM name are not carried by any wire and are not in any screener's positioning field; the FCA short register, which IS in the baseline, reads a truncated zero for this issuer and therefore says nothing. If it were priced, the baseline's positioning fields would not be three zeros. I size it small and positive rather than large because it is three months stale and because Rathbones cuts the other way.
evidence.independence: The Rathbones notification is a separate RNS: [url removed] (2026-07-07). The 39.73% concert party figure comes from a third document, the Notice of AGM / Rule 9 waiver circular: [url removed]

evidence.text: The GBP2.5m buyback is 89-98% spent and its bid disappears within about two weeks. Treasury reached 1,116,967 shares by 16 September; the 3 August tranche went at a 187.59p VWAP and everything after it traded in a 200-223p band, which bounds cumulative consideration at GBP2.22m-GBP2.46m of the GBP2.5m maximum. At the recent pace (86,371 shares in the week to 11 September, 50,685 in three days to 16 September) the authority is exhausted in early October, removing a buyer that has been ~19% of daily volume. Real and sourceable, and worth nothing to a one-session window.

The entire FY26 second-half case rests on events that settle after this print: the Dirk Rossmann pilot across 2,200 German stores (launched May 2026, reorder decision H2), the 'significantly improved' Walmart Christmas order, the Ulta Beauty online Christmas gift range, and Barry M's first re-sourced production run after the London factory was excluded from the acquisition. Christmas sell-through is a December/January fact.

Any RNS between the 16 June AGM statement and the print that pre-releases H1 numbers -- there is none. evidence.text: Myer's FY26 release on 22 Sep 2026 disclosed its first 8 weeks of FY27: Myer Apparel Brands (Just Jeans, Jay Jays, Portmans, Dotti, Jacqui E, the specialty mall chains Premier sold it) comparable sales -5.9% and total sales -6.0%, Myer Retail comps +1.8%, and a 'material downturn' in June-July. Premier habitually gives first-N-weeks brand sales at its full-year result (FY25: Peter Alexander +9.2%, Smiggle -4.0% in the first 6 weeks), so the FY27 read tomorrow is likely soft, especially against Lew's promise to return Smiggle to growth in FY27.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: First-weeks trading has driven PMV's results-day reactions. 1H26 on 20 Mar 2026: -4.31% even though Peter Alexander's first 7 weeks were said to exceed the 1H trend. FY25 on 25 Sep 2025: -0.15% on PA +9.2% and Smiggle -4.0% with a dividend described as a surprise. FY24 on 25 Sep 2024: -9.09%. The 12 Aug 2026 guidance cut: -11.01%. So soft commentary on this name has been sold hard, and good commentary has not been bought.
evidence.why_not_priced: PMV closed -0.88% on 22 Sep and -0.45% on 23 Sep, the two sessions after Myer's release: well inside its ordinary daily noise. Shorts sit flat at 1.27%. So nothing on the tape or the register reflects the Myer data being mapped onto Premier's first-weeks number. The mapping is a hypothesis: Premier's categories (sleepwear and gifting, kids' stationery) are not Myer's youth and women's apparel. That is why the size is small.
evidence.independence: Same direction, different sources: Accent Group like-for-like sales -2% in its first 7 weeks of FY27 (search summary citing August 2026 reporting-season coverage; primary URL not retrieved, so it is not load-bearing). Cutting against it: Myer's same release says August weakness improved in September on Father's Day promotions, and Father's Day is a Peter Alexander gifting event (same investing.com source).

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of OBSERVED prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. evidence.text: The FY26 accounts are the first set drawn up with market cap far below book. Net assets were US$203.2m at 31 Dec 2025, when the directors said 'no indicators for impairment' at a share price of A$0.645. Since then CY2026 guidance (400-500k lb) was withdrawn on 22 Jul, the Life-of-Mine plan has been withdrawn since Aug 2025, and market cap is about A$151m. That is a textbook AASB 136 indicator, so the annual report must at least carry a Lance CGU impairment test and may book a write-down. On top of that comes a second-half inventory write-down to net realisable value, following the US$8.4m one in H1 that came from capitalising full production cost onto small volumes.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Financial-statement lodgements have barely moved PEN. The half-year that carried the US$8.4m NRV write-down and a going-concern material uncertainty (09/03/2026 17:13) was followed by 0.0% on 10/03/2026. Annual reports went +2.63% (11/09/2024) and -2.68% (30/09/2025). PEN moves on operational news instead: -26.0% on the 22/07/2026 guidance withdrawal, +22.2% on the 31/07/2026 quarterly. No prior PEN impairment of the Lance CGU could be observed.
evidence.why_not_priced: The economic content is priced: at about 0.4-0.5x last-reported book the market already values Lance well below its carrying amount, which is why this is capped small. What the price has not had is the accounting event, plus whatever recoverable-amount assumptions the directors must now disclose with no LoM plan (flows, grades, costs). If the market expected an unpleasant disclosure you would see a building short. What the register shows is 1.47%, up only 0.13pp, and a +1.9% five-day tape. No coverage or preview of the FY26 accounts turned up in search.
evidence.independence: The withdrawn guidance and missing LoM plan come from a different document: the 22/07/2026 Operational and Production Guidance Update (https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260722/pdf/071y794hlm6qhj.pdf). The market-cap side rests on ASIC's short file (share count) and the Yahoo tape. The impairment itself is an inference, and no company statement says a write-down is coming.

evidence.text: MU-5 final investment decision. The 22/07/2026 update said 'expects to make a final investment decision ... in September 2026'; the 31/07 quarterly said 'before the end of CY2026'. evidence.text: Solaria's print-day reaction is structurally skewed upward over this window. The sell-side has repeatedly under-modelled its non-generation income: Q1-26 net profit was 80.4m against a 17m consensus, with 49.6m of infrastructure services against 25.8m of energy sales. The release lands in-session with a growth headline, while the call where quality gets questioned comes at 18:00 CET after the close. The stock closed up on D at each of the last five prints (+9.44% on 2025-06-03, +5.27% on 2025-09-30, +15.72% on 2025-11-17, +8.73% on 2026-02-26, +4.31% on 2026-05-18). Against Sabadell's 92m Q2 EBITDA bar, I expect a modest beat.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: D-day closes computed from Yahoo daily bars, with CNMV filing times. The last five in-session prints were all up: +9.44, +5.27, +15.72, +8.73, +4.31. The two 2024 post-close prints fell on D+1 (-7.58 on the 9M-24 profit cut, +1.83). The largest beat (Q1-26, NP 80 vs 17 est.) was +4.31 on D and then -6.34 on D+1 after the call, so beats are sold on digestion and only D counts here.
evidence.why_not_priced: Had the market priced a print-day pop, the stock would be running up into the release. Instead it is -1.9% over 20 days and -15.6% over 60, fell 3.7% on the seal day, is ~32% below its 26 May close of 24.47, and has disclosed shorts still at 5.6% with fresh quant shorts dated 18 and 21 September. The bar has already moved up after Q1: Sabadell's 92m Q2 EBITDA is +39% year on year. That leaves the edge thinner than in May, which is why the size is small.
evidence.independence: Partly independent: the reaction series is my own computation from Yahoo bars (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/SLR.MC?range=3y&interval=1d) timed by CNMV filings (https://www.cnmv.es/portal/otra-informacion-relevante/resultado-oir?nif=A83511501&page=2&lang=es). Arithmetic check: 113.2m Q1 EBITDA + 92m Q2 = ~62% of the ~330m FY target at H1 (https://quartr.com/events/solaria-energ-a-y-medio-ambiente-s-a-slr-q1-2026_oSpXaNRV), so the release can frame the year as ahead of plan. The firm said it would only update guidance at an undated H2 investor day.

evidence.text: The disclosed short book is 5.61% across seven holders on the live CNMV register. It is rotating from discretionary to quant holders into the print: Marshall Wace opened 0.82% on 21/09 and WorldQuant 0.59% on 18/09, while Parvus cut 1.02%->0.69% and AHL 0.90%->0.68% since August. On a headline beat that is about 7 days of volume to cover.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior read on squeezes. The Nov-2025 print (+15.72% on D) came while the stock was already rallying. Shorts built through Jul-Aug 2026 as the stock fell 35% (merca2, 12 Aug).
evidence.why_not_priced: The sealed baseline has no positioning at all (covered: false), so the stage's lean is just the run-up. The register is public, but the rotation (fundamental shorts trimming while quant books add in the last week) is only visible by diffing it against August press coverage. Had it been read as bearish conviction building, the stock would not have held 16-17.5 through September on flat volume.
evidence.independence: Rests on a different document from finding 1. The August baseline comes from merca2 (https://www.merca2.es/2026/08/12/solaria-posiciones-cortas-fondos-bajistas-2434929/): 5.1%, Parvus 1.02, AHL 0.90, CFM 0.81. The amplification depends on finding 1's beat landing, so the two are correlated in outcome, not in evidence.

Any decision will likely come at a Consejo de Ministros after the window, and it could reverse the move either way.

If the market had priced a freight-driven FY27 cut, the FY27 consensus on [THE COMPANY]'s own page would sit at or below FY26's £44.8m, not at £48.0m. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the line the name is repeatedly sold on. Last year's same quarter (Q1 FY2026, printed late September 2025) missed EPS by 2.8% and the baseline's cadence window records -6.16%. The FY2026 print on 2026-06-25 reported record revenue and cloud +34.3% but 経常 ¥91,373M against an IFIS consensus of ¥93,100M (-1.9%) and the stock closed 2026-06-26 at ¥8,088 against ¥8,223, -1.64%. evidence.why_not_priced: If the market had marked the bar to the run rate, the sell-side full-year consensus would not sit at OP +11.8% on revenue +7.1% — 470bp of operating leverage — nor at net income ¥70,150M, which is ¥1.0bn ABOVE the top of the company's own EPS guidance range of ¥540 (≈¥69.1bn). It would also not carry a ¥11,467 target price, 23% above spot, with a 4.0/5 average rating. The arithmetic runs the other way: holding gross margin flat at 45.0% and hitting consensus OP would require absolute operating expenses to FALL about 4% after a year in which they rose 11.2%, and cloud rising to roughly 35% of revenue makes flat gross margin itself optimistic.

It is at 506 now, below the 550 of the July 8 close and far below 626 in June. If the margin step-up were priced, the stock would have re-rated off the placement price toward Ipopema's 650-670 targets rather than drifting 455-512 through September. Only one broker covers the name. Counter-weights: the +4.98% 5-day run-up, and the absence of any sourced EBITDA bar, mean this is capped.

The H1 report may quantify this, but the revenue effect falls in H2.

evidence.text: The FY2027/2 company plan the whole market is anchored on (revenue 862.78億 +6.0%, OP 43.0億 +9.2%) requires roughly +7.5% revenue growth across the remaining nine months after a Q1 that grew 3%, at a time when the company has explicitly told investors it is suppressing new store openings under VISION2028 and its own published monthly existing-store series is running around flat -- and IFIS consensus 経常 for the year is 4,440百万, exactly the company number, so no analyst has marked the plan down.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line that moves this stock, and it moves it hard when it is cut: the 2025-12-22 業績予想の修正 (revenue 858億 to 810億, OP 56.2億 to 42.3億) drove the shares down in the afternoon session and again the following day ('後場下げ幅を拡大', then '続落'), and the baseline's estimated December-2024 reaction is -6.42%. Reported-quarter surprises by contrast have been looked through: the FY2026/2 result on 2026-04-03 missed IFIS 経常 consensus by 5.3% and the stock set its 2026 high of 1,457 that day because the new mid-term plan landed with it. The estimated September reactions are small and mixed (-3.36, +1.87, +1.67).
evidence.why_not_priced: If the market had marked the plan down, the sell-side 経常 number would not be byte-identical to the company's own 4,440百万 -- on a name with this little coverage the consensus is the company guide with the sign changed, and there is nothing else for a screen to read. It is also not in the tape as a directional bet: run_up_20d is only -2.79%, there is no disclosed short at the 0.5% threshold on the JPX register, and 信用倍率 3.16 says retail is long, not positioned for a disappointment. What would look different if this were priced: a visible gap between consensus and guidance, or a disclosed short balance, or a 20-day run-in materially worse than -3%.
evidence.independence: The suppression of new openings and the DOE-3%/payout-35% return policy that the plan rests on come from a different document, the VISION2028 mid-term plan coverage at [url removed] ; the Q1 revenue and cost figures come from Nikkei's 2026-06-22 report at [url removed] . Note this finding shares its underlying thesis with finding 2 below -- both say the FY plan is out of reach -- and they should be read as one direction, not two independent confirmations.

evidence.text: H1 operating profit is set to fall high-single to low-double digits year on year, because Q2 (May 21-Aug 20) is this company's thinnest-margin quarter -- prior-year Q2 standalone OP was only about 5.4億 on about 190億 of revenue, a ~2.8% margin, derived from H1 OP 37億 less Q1 OP ~31.6億 -- and Q1 already carried +8% personnel cost growth from wage rises and hiring plus new-store depreciation against revenue growth of just 3%, so a near-flat Q2 revenue line converts into a Q2 OP roughly half of last year's.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This stock has repeatedly not punished a weak reported half. The 2025-09 H1 print (revenue 459億 -1%, OP 37億 -21%, net 26億 -19%) sits on the estimated cadence as a +1.67% reaction, and the 2026-04-03 full-year print missed consensus 経常 by 5.3% and closed at the year's high. The reported quarter is not where this name's risk premium sits.
evidence.why_not_priced: Honestly, most of this IS priced: the Q1 release is three months old and every month of H1 has been published as a 月次 by 2026-09-03, so any reader who wants the revenue line already has it. What is less well modelled on a one-analyst name is the operating leverage arithmetic -- that an 8% cost line growing against a 2.8%-margin quarter halves the quarter's profit -- and that is why this is [sizing note removed]. If it were fully priced, the consensus 経常 would already sit below the company number, and it does not.
evidence.independence: The Q1 cost and revenue detail is a separate Nikkei report, [url removed] (2026-06-22). Pointing the OTHER way, and recorded here rather than buried: direct competitor DAIWA CYCLE (5888) released H1 (Feb-Jul 2026) results and an August sales flash on 2026-09-14 reporting record half-year sales and operating profit ([url removed] after a Q1 of revenue 69.6億 +12.3% and OP 6.56億 +7.3%, so the category through July was not weak and [THE COMPANY]'s problem is company-specific cost and share, not collapsing demand. That counterweight is why the high end of this range is positive.

evidence.text: The pattern that actually resizes this stock is a 業績予想の修正 filed in December, not at H1 -- the 2025-12-22 cut took revenue from 858億 to 810億 and OP from 56.2億 to 42.3億 and was sold hard. If the FY2027/2 plan is unreachable on the arithmetic above, the most likely date the market sees it confirmed is the Q3 print or a separate revision around late December 2026, months after this exit.

evidence.text: Tullow's own H1 production (c.43.7 kboepd) is already above the top of its 34-42 kboepd FY range. The operator's partner Kosmos reported Jubilee exiting Q2 above 85k bopd gross, with J50 expected to lift it above 90k bopd. That puts Tullow's Q3 net run-rate near 50 kboepd (c.39% of 90k Jubilee + c.8 TEN + c.7.5 gas). The Aug guide of 'high end of 34-42' looks mechanically too low, so a production raise above the range at the interims is likely.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance-bearing Tullow updates move a lot and in both directions. The FCF upgrade in the 2026-08-05 Trading Statement went to -6.66% (the market focused on flat net debt, per Jefferies via Investing.com). The June 2026 AGM update with 'higher end' language went +8.84%. The H1 2025 results with a guide cut went -18.99%. The last results day after a pre-release trading statement (FY, 2026-04-28) went +11.40%, but the refinancing completion landed the same day. H1 2024 results went +0.87%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Tullow has repeated 'high end of 34-42' three times (FY results, AGM update, Aug TS) while printing above 42 each time, so any model anchored on company language sits at 42 or below. If the market had priced a range raise, the reaction to the 5 Aug statement would not have been -6.7%. Most of the 60-day rally lines up with Brent (80 to about 107 at peak) and with Kosmos moving in step, not with a Tullow-specific volume rerating. Caveat: Kosmos is a public, well-read source and analysts can do this arithmetic, so most of it is probably known. That is why the size is small.
evidence.independence: Tullow's own 5 Aug RNS: H1 43.7 kboepd, J76 'significantly above expectations', J77 and J50 onstream (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/tullow-oil--tlw/trading-statement/9704842). evidence.text: The FY26 FCF guide ($170-250m at $70-100/bbl) rests on Jan-Jul realisations of c.$93/bbl. Brent front-month traded roughly $88-109 from mid-August to 24 Sep. The company states a sensitivity of about +$30m FCF per +$10/bbl above $80, so the interims are likely to firm the guide toward or above the top of the range.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last FCF upgrade (2026-08-05, from $70-175m to $170-250m) was sold: -6.66% on the day. The June AGM update with FCF upside framing went +8.84%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The stock is up about 43% since 14 Aug alongside Brent, and oil is a public series. What stays unpriced is only the step from 'implied' to 'company-stated'. Brent fell about 7% on 25 Sep (106.60 to 98.82, Yahoo BZ=F), which cools the read-through before the window opens. This finding and the first one both land on the same guidance line, so together they count as one guide raise and are sized that way.

evidence.text: The April 2026 refinancing requires an M&A process to begin before end-2026; if no binding SPA follows within nine months (by 30 Sep 2027), the New Notes' maturity springs forward to 15 May 2028. It could be launched with the interims, but the equity sign is ambiguous: creditors rank first on proceeds, and it could still bring a takeover premium. Timing in the window is unknown, so it is sized 0.

evidence.text: PKP CARGO's Q2 2026 ton-km looks to be up about +19% YoY, from about +10% in Q1. The cumulative headlines read as falling share (mass share YTD 27.84% after March, 27.13% after June), and that masks the Q2 year-on-year gain. Derived from UTK cumulative shares times market totals: Q2 2026 about 3.96bn tkm against about 3.34bn in Q2 2025, and Q2 mass share about 26.5% against about 25.1%. The Q2 2025 EBITDA base it lands on is weak at 65.4m PLN (H1 140.2m less Q1 74.8m).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent on an EBITDA surprise. H1 2025 was +7.33% on 2025-10-01 on a net-profit headline. FY2025 was +4.41% on 2026-04-29. Q3 2025 was about 0% on 2025-12-01. Q1 2026 was -14.19% on 2026-06-01, confounded because debt-to-equity conversion and a rights issue at 12 PLN were announced the same evening.
evidence.why_not_priced: Each monthly PAP wire reports a cumulative share that has fallen month after month since March. It is never de-cumulated into a quarterly volume, so the Q2 acceleration shows up in no headline. With one analyst and no published estimate there is no consensus EBITDA to carry it. If it were priced, the stock would not sit 13% below the 12 PLN rights-issue floor with a -3.5% 20-day drift into the print. That said, the drawdown is more plausibly dilution than operations, which is why this is sized small.
evidence.independence: Same UTK series from different PAP months. Mass after March 2026 was 27.65% (revised to 27.84%) against 26.91%, and ton-km 28.31% against 25.93%: https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/Udzial-PKP-Cargo-w-rynku-przewiezionych-towarow-wg-masy-wzrosl-rdr-po-III-do-27-65-proc-UTK-9125670.html. Market totals for H1 2026 (107.4mt, +2.3%): https://www.rynek-kolejowy.pl/wiadomosci/przewozy-towarowe-czwarty-z-rzedu-miesiac-poprawy-polrocze-na-plusie-153927.html. Against it: the company's own Q1 form shows revenue of 924.7m against 939.6m on about +10% ton-km (https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/PKP-CARGO-S-A-W-RESTRUKTURYZACJI-Wyniki-finansowe-QSr-1-2026-9142747.html). Volume is being bought with price, and that is why the size is cut.

evidence.text: The H1 2026 net result will be compared against an H1 2025 figure (-17.9m PLN) that contained a Q2 2025 net profit of +30.7m. StockWatch attributed that profit mainly to a reversal of write-downs (odwrócenie odpisów). With Q1 2026 already at -45.8m, H1 2026 matches last year only if Q2 2026 nets more than about +28m, so the likely wire headline is a wider half-year loss. That would also sit awkwardly against the strategy's line that the group returns to net profit in 2026.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last time the net headline surprised was H1 2025: the one-off-driven Q2 profit printed and the stock rose +7.33% on 2025-10-01 on 354k shares, against about 30k typical. So this name has reacted to the headline net number rather than to its quality.
evidence.why_not_priced: Nobody publishes an H1 net estimate for this name: the baseline shows 1 analyst and a null estimate. The prior-year one-off is a year-old footnote, not something a wire comparison adjusts for. If the market had already framed H1 2026 against a clean base, there would be sell-side or press previews saying so, and I found none. Still, Q1's -45.8m is public and the stock is at 52-week lows, so a good part of 'still loss-making' is already in the price. Hence the small size.
evidence.independence: H1 2025 figures (EBIT 54.7m, net -17.9m, Q2 net +30.7m) from a different outlet: https://kolejowyportal.pl/grupa-pkp-cargo-przedstawila-wyniki-za-i-polrocze-2025-roku/. Q1 2026 net -45.8m: https://kolejowyportal.pl/pkp-cargo-podsumowalo-pierwszy-kwartal-2026-roku/. The strategy line on net profitability in 2026: https://www.pkpcargo.com/raporty_biezace/zatwierdzenie-przez-rade-nadzorcza-strategii-restrukturyzacyjnej-grupy-kapitalowej-pkp-cargo-na-lata-2025-2031/. This does not contradict finding 1: EBITDA can rise year on year while net falls against a base that one-off reversals flattered.

evidence.text: The creditors' council's opinion on the 15 September arrangement proposals, and the deadline for competing proposals from parties other than PKP CARGO or the administrator, both fall on 2026-10-15. The creditor vote follows. This is the event that actually sets the equity's fate.

Series N rights issue of 75.0-89.6m shares at the higher of 12.00 PLN or 80% of the 50-session VWAP ending 2026-12-16. That floor is above today's 10.42 spot, so on current prices the rights are out of the money. Add 29.4m series D shares converting Group IV state-railway claims at 12 PLN (44.8m -> 74.2m shares before N) and warrants letting PKP S.A. hold 25-33.34%. The dilution is known and was announced on 2026-05-29/06-23.

The PLN 1.52bn 'coal decision' damages claim against the State Treasury. The regional court resumed it and suspended it again on 2026-09-15 for settlement talks, and the 15/09 proposals hand 50% of any net recovery to creditor groups I, III and IV. It is undated and, as a contingent asset, will not appear in the H1 balance sheet.

If a cut were priced, shorts would be adding and the price would sit at or below the May low. options.reason: No liquid single-stock option market in Japan for this name. JPX option volume is concentrated in the index, so there is no event-implied move and no skew. Until 2026-09-18 that left priced_lean_pct as -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, which is ALSO the free control, so the baseline's lean and its own benchmark were the same number. They are no longer: `positioning` and `expected_move` below carry substitutes built from what Tokyo does publish, and this baseline supplies its own `priced_lean_pct` and `anchor_quality`.

history.caveat: Announcement DATES are estimated by applying this quarter's notified lag backwards to prior period ends; the move is the largest within +/-2 trading days of that estimate. This is a cadence prior, not a record that a print happened on that date. Use it as a scale for how much this name moves, never as evidence about a particular past date.

event_plausibility.basis: issuer-notified date carried by JPX on the 決算発表予定日 sheet

positioning.basis: absent from the JPX register, so no disclosed position at or above the 0.5% threshold. A real zero, not missing data -- but the threshold truncates, so 0.4% and 0.0% are both recorded here as 0.0.
positioning.margin_ratio_basis: 信用倍率, margin long balance / margin short balance, scraped from a broker portal rather than published by the exchange. Null is a normal outcome.

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of twelve ESTIMATED prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it, and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read researcher_japan/scripts/jp_priced_in.py, lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR, none is measured on Japanese data, and jp_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters today is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

anchor_quality.basis: magnitude: realised vol plus an estimated-cadence reaction history, capped at 0.5 because neither is an option-implied move. direction: how many of the three positioning components resolved, capped at 0.60 because none of them is 25-delta skew.

evidence.text: The FY2026/5 決算短信 shows the order backlog at 2026-05-31 up 23.0% YoY: total 7,979百万円 against 6,488, disclosure segment 7,969 against 6,470 (+1,499), and 金商法関連 (有報 etc.) 4,706 against 3,465 (+35.8%). Orders ran +10.7%, yet Q4 (Mar-May) sales grew only +2.2%. The work was booked but not yet billed going into the June 有報 peak, which falls in Q1 (Jun-Aug). A year earlier the backlog fell 2.8% and Q1 still grew sales +8.6%. So Q1 FY27 sales of ~+9-12% and OP of ~+12-22% (progress ~40-42% of 4,900, against 38.7% last year) are the likely outcome. Net of the peer read-through below.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Actual release dates are from kabutan, and each move runs from the D close (15:30) to the D+1 close off Yahoo daily bars. Q1 FY26 (2025-09-29): sales +8.6% and OP +3.7%, below that year's +8.7% OP guide pace; D -0.24%, then -2.36%. Q1 FY25 (2024-09-30): OP down YoY; -2.58% next session (the Yahoo D-1 bar for that date looks corrupt). Other prints ran -0.70%, +0.32%, +1.56% and +1.20%. The two guide/dividend prints moved +3.35% and +8.03% (the latter after +18% in the final 30 minutes of D). Quarterly beats have not been bought much; the FY guide line moves this stock.
evidence.why_not_priced: The headline on 07-08 was the +60 yen dividend and the 中期経営計画2029 (kabutan: '今期は営業益11%増を計画し年間配当予想は60円増配'). The 受注残高 table sits on page 3 of the 短信. No analyst covers the name, so nothing turns it into a Q1 estimate. Since then the stock has given back its post-results high (4,395 on 08-28 to 4,045) on 優待 disappointment, and the Yahoo board argues about 優待 and 配当, not orders. If the backlog were priced, the pre-print drift would be up rather than -6% over 20 days, and holders would be discussing the Q1 progress rate.
evidence.independence: Cross-checked against last year's backlog table (FY2025/5 決算短信, https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20250709/140120250708509794.pdf: backlog -2.8% at 2025-05-31, followed by Q1 sales +8.6%) and the Q4 sales from kabutan's 3-month table (https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=7921). Those are two readings from the company's own documents, so they count once. The one different-source datum points the other way: Pronexus (7893) Q1 Apr-Jun 2026 (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260731/140120260730503996.pdf) shows sales +5.3%, mostly from M&A, and OP +0.4%. 招集通知 revenue fell (about 90 fewer listed companies, electronic provision cutting print pages) and English translation orders fell. That drag is already netted into the +1.0; without it I would size about +1.5. A primary company document beats an industry proxy, so the peer read cuts the size but does not flip the sign.

evidence.text: The Q1 over-delivery (OP ¥11.37bn against an implied Q1 plan of ~¥9.70bn, +¥1.68bn) exceeds the likely Q2 shortfall implied by the published 月次 (Q2 existing-store -10.7/-1.8/-0.2, all-store -5.4/+4.3/+6.0). So H1 OP most likely lands around ¥20.5-21.5bn against the ¥20.2bn plan (H1 経常 ~¥19.9bn against ¥19.3bn, roughly flat YoY), a 'plan beaten' H1 print carrying a Q2 standalone OP decline of about 5-20% YoY.
evidence.source_date: 2026-09-08 (page 最終更新日; August 2026 速報)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Actual close-to-next-close reactions from Yahoo bars on the kabutan-listed release dates: H1 FY26 (2025-09-26, OP 94.7% of plan) -0.96%; Q1 FY27 (2026-06-26, OP 117.3% of plan) +4.44%, fully reversed by 2026-07-01 (1,575 to 1,484); FY26 (2026-04-14) -4.46%; others -2.05, -3.17, -1.99, +1.43. 5 of 7 negative at the close, though 5 of 7 opened higher. Beats get bought at the open and sold into the session.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly it is priced, and that is why the size is small. The 月次 are syndicated (ryutsuu 2026-09-14) and the 117.3%-of-plan Q1 figure is in the Q1 supplement. If the market feared an H1 miss after June's -10.7%, the stock would sit near the 1,480 post-June-monthly level. It trades at 1,589, back near its post-Q1 high. The unpriced residue is only the size of the cushion: few readers do the Q1-plan against Q2-shortfall arithmetic on a thinly covered name, and Q2's Enchō drag (about -¥0.8bn a quarter in Q1, and not in last year's Q2 base) is the swing item.
evidence.independence: The progress-rate arithmetic comes from a different document: the Q1 supplement https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260626/140120260626581136.pdf (plan ratios, Enchō -793 OP bridge) and last year's H1 supplement https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20250926/140120250926563086.pdf (Q2 FY26 OP 11,158 on existing-store -4.3%, showing DCM can hold Q2 profit on falling comps via cost control). Both come from the company, so they are not independent in the strict sense. Counter-evidence: Nafco's Apr-Jun OP fell 6.7% on sales up 0.8% (https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=2790&b=k202608070351), a sign the June payback hurt home-center margins.

evidence.text: September 2026 月次, the first read on whether the stockpiling payback has ended and whether H2's implied plan (FY OP ¥31.2bn less H1) is reachable, publishes in early October.

positioning.basis: ASIC's aggregated daily short position report. NOT a 0.5% disclosure register: every product with a reported position appears, and 430 of 755 rows on 2026-09-16 were below 0.5%. expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of OBSERVED prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it says nothing about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Unlike stage J's, the history half rests on real announcement dates.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. anchor_quality.basis: magnitude: realised vol plus an OBSERVED reaction history, capped because neither is an option-implied move. direction: how many of the two positioning components resolved off ASIC's untruncated daily register, capped because neither is skew. positioning.basis: absent from a register that downloaded successfully, so no disclosed net short position at or above the 0.5% public threshold. A real zero -- but the threshold truncates, so 0.4% and 0.0% are both recorded here as 0.0, and the join is on the issuer NAME, so a name spelled differently in the register reads as a zero it should not.

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Phase 1 median realised move was 2.81% (UK), 3.12% (DE), 4.19% (FR) against Japan's 2.87%, with the tail intact in all three -- 42%, 27% and 52% maxima and no price limit to truncate them.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read eu_priced_in.lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR borrowed from the US runs, none is measured on European data, and eu_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

options.reason: No liquid single-stock option market in Japan for this name. JPX option volume is concentrated in the index, so there is no event-implied move and no skew. Until 2026-09-18 that left priced_lean_pct as -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, which is ALSO the free control, so the baseline's lean and its own benchmark were the same number. They are no longer: `positioning` and `expected_move` below carry substitutes built from what Tokyo does publish, and this baseline supplies its own `priced_lean_pct` and `anchor_quality`.

history.caveat: Announcement DATES are estimated by applying this quarter's notified lag backwards to prior period ends; the move is the largest within +/-2 trading days of that estimate. This is a cadence prior, not a record that a print happened on that date. Use it as a scale for how much this name moves, never as evidence about a particular past date.

event_plausibility.basis: issuer-notified date carried by JPX on the 決算発表予定日 sheet

positioning.basis: sum of disclosed positions at or above 0.5% of shares outstanding, aggregated over sellers
positioning.margin_ratio_basis: 信用倍率, margin long balance / margin short balance, scraped from a broker portal rather than published by the exchange. Null is a normal outcome.

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of twelve ESTIMATED prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it, and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read researcher_japan/scripts/jp_priced_in.py, lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR, none is measured on Japanese data, and jp_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. evidence.text: H1 operating profit is tracking ~11bn (Q1 actual 7,875m plus a Q2 estimate of 2.9-3.9bn), about 63-68% of the unchanged 17.2bn FY guide. The guide therefore implies H2 OP of ~6bn against 8.55bn last year. The company raised its FY guide at H1 the last time it ran this far ahead (2023-09-29, OP 14.0->18.0bn), so an upward revision at this print is more likely than not. The Q2 estimate comes from the TDnet monthly: parent-company Q2 sales +0.9%, same-store -0.8%, customers -2.2%, but same-store ticket +1.5% (Aug +4.0%), which is the markdown-restraint pattern that lifted Q1 gross margin +1.3pt against a Q2 last year at ~53.7% GM / 3.3% OP margin after inventory clearance.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 (2026-06-30): OP +40.5%, ordinary 8.05bn vs ~6.75bn consensus, guide held -> next session -2.74% after a +5.6% two-day run-in (kabutan n202607010368, '織り込み済み'). H1 FY2026 (2025-09-30): H1 ordinary -24%, below consensus, guide held -> -7.61% (baseline; Nikkei DGXZQOFL010T00R01C25A0000000). H1 FY2025 (2024-09-30): guide held at 19.0bn -> +6.45% (baseline, estimated date). The last H1 raise, 2023-09-29 (kabuyoho revision history), is outside the baseline window.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at 19.4bn ordinary already assumes a raise, so the revision is only partly news. What is not in the price is the stock holding that view: before Q1 it ran +5.6% in two days and sat at 3,460-3,525, but it has now fallen from 3,555 (08-26) to 3,065, ~4-5pt worse than apparel peers after the dividend, while consensus rose 2.3% on 09-10 and the average target is 3,557. At 13.5x company EPS the stock is trading as though the guide will be held, or Q2 will disappoint on the June -6.2% same-store month. If the raise were priced it would sit near the pre-Q1 level, not 14% below it.
evidence.independence: Same fundamental read, separate source: the kabuyoho/IFIS consensus rose from 18,925m to 19,375m on 2026-09-10 (https://kabuyoho.jp/reportTop?bcode=2685), and a Nikkei 2026-09-05 headline has a director citing reduced markdown sales (https://www.nikkei.com/nkd/company/news/?scode=2685, headline only, paywalled). Against it: Shimamura's Jun-Aug OP margin fell 9.2%->8.7% and its FY guide was held on 2026-09-28 (https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=8227&b=k202609280002), a sign that summer-quarter apparel margins were under FX/cost pressure. That is why the low end sits at -2.5.

history.caveat: Announcement DATES are estimated by applying this quarter's notified lag backwards to prior period ends; the move is the largest within +/-2 trading days of that estimate.
